### B. Core Implementations & Technical Details







1. **Dependency Injection & Manifest Permissions**:



   - `build.gradle.kts`: Added `implementation("org.osmdroid:osmdroid-android:6.1.18")`.



   - `AndroidManifest.xml`: Declared network and storage caching permissions:



     - `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />`



     - `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE" />`



     - `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />`



2. **Native Map Configuration (`ClassMateTransitScreen.kt`)**:



   - Initialized `Configuration.getInstance().userAgentValue = context.packageName` to comply with OpenStreetMap tile usage policies.



   - Configured `MapView`: multi-touch pinch zoom, built-in zoom controls disabled, software rendering fallback configured for legacy GPU hardware, and tiles cached in app private storage (`context.cacheDir/osmdroid`).



   - Default viewport centered on MBSTU Santosh Campus coordinates (`24.2384° N, 89.8922° E`, zoom level 15.5).



3. **OkHttp Engine.IO v4 Protocol Implementation**:



   - Established persistent WebSocket to `wss://transport.mbstu.ac.bd/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket`.



   - On `onMessage`:



     - If message starts with `"0"`: parses `pingInterval` and immediately transmits `"40"` string to bind default namespace.



     - If message equals `"2"`: immediately responds with `"3"`.



     - If message starts with `"42"`: decodes `[eventName, payload]`. Maps `flutter-bus-data` and `studentGpsData` into native `MbstuBus` data classes and dispatches updates to main thread via `Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())`.



   - Automatic reconnection: Exponential backoff ($1\text{s}, 2\text{s}, 4\text{s}, 8\text{s}$, max $30\text{s}$) upon network loss or server socket reset.



4. **Hardware Concurrency & Backend Relay Roadmap**:



   - *Direct Connection Risk*: If hundreds of ClassMate students open the app simultaneously during peak dismissal hours ($01:30\text{ PM}, 04:30\text{ PM}$), hundreds of concurrent WebSocket connections could trigger IP rate-limiting or firewall bans on the university server.



   - *Backend Relay Solution*: Route telemetry through a centralized backend server or Supabase Edge Function that maintains a single upstream connection to `transport.mbstu.ac.bd` and fans out updates to connected clients using Supabase Realtime Channels or lightweight Server-Sent Events (SSE).

## 166. Live-Only Telemetry Ingestion, Geolocation Range Calculation, Auto-Adapting Corridor Bounds & High-Contrast Bus Marker Hardening (Commit `a3af691`)







### A. Architectural Intent & Elimination of Stale Mock Artifacts







Prior to this update, the transit engine relied on cached fleet snapshots stored in `localStorage` (`classmate_mbstu_fleet`) to provide zero-latency initial UI rendering. However, this caused significant user confusion: stale mock positions and inactive buses were displayed on the map even when university transport was not actively operating.







The user explicitly mandated a **live-only tracking policy**:



1. **Stale Cache Elimination**: Completely purged `localStorage.removeItem("classmate_mbstu_fleet")` on component mount.



2. **Authentic Sensor Telemetry**: The UI strictly renders vehicles for which active, authentic GPS packets are received from `wss://transport.mbstu.ac.bd/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket` within valid Bangladesh coordinate bounds (20° < lat < 28°, 85° < lon < 95°).



3. **Empty State Transparency**: When no buses are active on campus, the screen displays a dedicated status message explaining that the live telemetry socket is connected and awaiting university bus dispatch, alongside a button to toggle an interactive road demo (`toggleDemoMode`) if desired.







---







### B. User Geolocation Range Calculation & Map Localization







The footer of the bus vehicle cards previously suffered from redundant status text (e.g. "GPS ????????" rendered twice in separate pills). This was overhauled with real-time user-to-bus proximity measurement:







```mermaid



flowchart LR



    A["User Device GPS<br>(navigator.geolocation)"] --> B["userLocation State<br>(lat, lon)"]



    C["Vehicle Telemetry<br>(WebSocket Socket.IO)"] --> D["bus.lat, bus.lon"]



    B --> E["Haversine Formula<br>(getDistanceMeters)"]



    D --> E



    E --> F["Card Footer Badge<br>?? ????? ???? X.X ????"]



    B --> G["Leaflet User Marker<br>(Royal Blue Dot + Pulse Wave)"]



    H["Floating Action Button<br>(transit-fab-btn)"] --> I["map.flyTo(userLocation, 16)"]



```







1. **Geolocation Sensor Polling (`navigator.geolocation.watchPosition`)**:



   - Configured with `{ enableHighAccuracy: true, maximumAge: 10000, timeout: 10000 }`.



   - Safely updates `userLocation` state without triggering unnecessary re-renders of the tile layer.



   - If location access is not yet permitted, the card displays an interactive pill: `?? ?????? ?????` (`.transit-request-loc-pill`), allowing the user to initiate the permission prompt via direct tap.



2. **Live Map User Marker (`.transit-user-marker`)**:



   - Custom `L.divIcon` rendered at `[userLocation.lat, userLocation.lon]` with `zIndexOffset: 1500`.



   - **Styling**: Centered 14px solid royal blue dot (`.transit-user-marker-dot`, `#2563eb`) with a 2.5px white border and drop shadow, surrounded by an expanding animated ripple pulse (`.transit-user-marker-pulse`, `transitUserPulse` keyframe expanding to 2.2x scale with decaying opacity).



   - Bound interactive popup: `?? ????? ??????? (You are here)`.



3. **Locate Me FAB (`.transit-fab-btn`)**:



   - Added a dedicated Floating Action Button alongside the MBSTU Campus reset button.



   - Uses `Lucide` `Navigation` compass icon tinted green (`#10b981`) when `userLocation` is locked.



   - On tap: smoothly executes `map.flyTo([userLocation.lat, userLocation.lon], 16, { animate: true, duration: 0.8 })`.







---







### C. Auto-Adapting Road Corridor Camera Window







To maintain spatial context without jarring camera snaps or fighting manual user gestures:



- **Throttled Panning**: The camera tracker enforces a 2.6-second throttle window (`lastCameraPanRef`) so user pinch-to-zoom and dragging interactions are not aggressively overridden.



- **Corridor Projection & Forward Sampling**:



  - Locates the active bus's nearest vertex on `REAL_STREET_POLYLINE` using `findClosestPolylineIndex`.



  - Samples the forward 18-20 polyline vertices along the vehicle's heading direction.



  - Combines these coordinates with the next approaching bus stoppage (`nextApproachingStopInfo.station`).



  - Calls `map.fitBounds(bounds, { paddingTopLeft: [75, 30], paddingBottomRight: [50, 30], maxZoom: 17, animate: true })`.



- **Result**: As the vehicle travels from Santosh Campus through Kagmari toward Tangail Nirala, the viewport continuously leads the bus, presenting upcoming turns and stations rather than showing passed terrain.







---







### D. High-Contrast Bus Marker Hardening & Rendering Engine







User feedback highlighted that earlier bus markers faded into the vector tile background and appeared washed out:



- **Enlarged Canvas**: Marker size expanded to 44x48px with a 42px diameter teardrop round badge.



- **100% Solid Opaque Foundation**: `background: #ffffff !important` with 3.5px solid border in the vehicle's designated brand color (`var(--bus-color)`).



- **Dual Protective Shadows**: `box-shadow: 0 4px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.65), inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.95)`.



- **Elimination of Stale De-saturation**: Removed `.is-stale { opacity: 0.65; filter: grayscale(0.5); }` rules. All markers maintain 100% opacity and vibrant contrast regardless of packet age.



- **Hardware-Accelerated CSS Glide**: `.transit-bus-marker-container { transition: transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); }` delivers smooth marker glides along the street network as GPS coordinates stream in.

---







### B. Phantom Hardware IMEI Tracker Elimination







#### The Telemetry Leak



The university transport server (`wss://transport.mbstu.ac.bd`) broadcasts multiple real-time Socket.IO events. While `flutter-bus-data` delivers structured bus objects, secondary events like `student-gps-data` broadcast raw hardware GPS packets originating from device testing boards, individual student trackers, or unassigned vehicle transponders.







These packets contain arbitrary 10 to 15-digit IMEI strings (e.g. `353701091171104`, `9175769656`, `7826087352`) without corresponding bus identities or route assignments. Previously, fallback logic assigned these packets default labels like `"MBSTU ??? (353701091171104)"`, cluttering the vehicle list and map with non-existent ghost vehicles.







#### Strict Ingestion Gatekeeper (`transit.tsx`)



A multi-layered whitelist filter was implemented:



1. **Event Whitelist**: Completely dropped the raw `student-gps-data` event listener; restricted exclusively to verified `flutter-bus-data` and `studentGpsData` events.



2. **Strict Identity Validation**:



   ```typescript



   const rawId = String(raw.id || raw.busId || raw.bus_id || "").toUpperCase().trim();



   const nameFromPacket = String(raw.busName || raw.nameBn || raw.name || "").trim();







   // Resolve against recognized university fleet catalog



   let info = rawId ? KNOWN_BUS_INFO[rawId] : undefined;



   let resolvedId = rawId;







   if (!info && nameFromPacket) {



     const matchKey = Object.keys(KNOWN_BUS_INFO).find(



       (k) => KNOWN_BUS_INFO[k].nameBn === nameFromPacket || nameFromPacket.includes(KNOWN_BUS_INFO[k].nameBn)



     );



     if (matchKey) {



       info = KNOWN_BUS_INFO[matchKey];



       if (!resolvedId || !resolvedId.startsWith("SB")) resolvedId = matchKey;



     }



   }







   // STRICT GATEKEEPER:



   // Must either begin with official "SB" identifier (SB0001-SB0010) OR match a verified Bengali bus name.



   // Unrecognized numeric IMEIs and rogue transponders are immediately dropped!



   if (!info && (!resolvedId || !resolvedId.startsWith("SB"))) {



     return; // Discard phantom tracker packet!



   }



   ```



3. **Fleet Catalog Expansion**:



   - Added `SB0005`: `"???????"` (*Shangshaptak*, `#8b5cf6`, `"MBSTU Transport Corridor"`).



   - Standardized `SB0007`: `"????????"` (*Dhaleshwari*, `#10b981`, `"Campus ? Tangail Old Bus Stand"`).







---







### C. Direct Web URL Hash Routing Parity (`app.tsx`)







In `web/src/components/app.tsx`, the route dispatch listener was updated to include `"transit"`:



```typescript



if (



  [



    "routine",



    "bus",



    "calendar",



    "notices",



    "batch",



    "fund",



    "profile",



    "manage",



    "ai",



    "transit" // Added direct hash navigation support



  ].includes(targetTab)



) {



  // Sets active tab to transit without defaulting back to routine



}



```



This enables direct deep-linking to `https://classmatebd.vercel.app/#transit` from mobile bookmarks, Telegram channels, and Android companion web views.







---







### D. Native Android APK Implementation Guidelines







To maintain full architectural parity between the web companion and native Android APK:



1. **Telemetry Ingestion Gatekeeper (`TelemetryParser.kt`)**:



   - Enforce the identical IMEI whitelist logic in Android's OkHttp `WebSocketListener`. Packets where `id` does not match the official `SB` regex (`^SB[0-9]{4}$`) or a recognized Bangla name must be discarded before dispatching to `LiveData<List<MbstuBus>>`.

## 168. Map Callout Blinking Elimination, Geolocation Origin Permission & Rich Telemetry Integration







### 168.1 Incident Diagnosis & Root Cause Analysis



1. **Map Callout Blinking / Flashing Strobe Effect**:



   - **Trigger**: Every 1000ms, the internal `clockNow` timer in `transit.tsx` updated `displayFleet` object references.



   - **Root Cause**: In `transit.tsx`, the bus marker update loop unconditionally executed `marker.setIcon(icon)` every single second. In Leaflet, calling `setIcon` destroys the marker's existing DOM subtree and rebuilds it from scratch.



   - **Visual Artifact**: Because `.transit-bus-callout` had `animation: calloutPop 0.22s cubic-bezier(...)` starting at `opacity: 0`, every time the DOM element was recreated, the animation restarted from `opacity: 0`, causing the callout bubble to blink/flash every second like a strobe light.



2. **Geolocation Permission Not Prompting**:



   - **Root Cause**: `web/next.config.ts` was sending `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=()`. Under modern browser security specifications, specifying `geolocation=()` completely blocks the Geolocation API at the HTTP header level. Browsers threw a permissions policy violation and refused to show the permission dialog.



3. **Map Floating Action Buttons (FAB) Bloat**:



   - The map action stack contained 4 buttons:



     1. `LocateFixed`: Selected bus focal tracker. (Useful)



     2. `Layers`: Google Satellite vs Roadmap layer toggle. (Useful)



     3. `MapPin`: Arbitrary recenter on MBSTU campus coordinates (24.2376°N, 89.8913°E). (Redundant/Useless)



     4. `Navigation`: User live locator. (Useful)







### 168.2 Architectural Resolutions Applied



1. **Zero-Blink DOM Stabilization in Leaflet**:



   - Stored `__renderedHtml` hash on the Leaflet marker instance:



     ```ts



     if ((marker as any).__renderedHtml !== html) {



       marker.setIcon(icon);



       (marker as any).__renderedHtml = html;



     }



     marker.setLatLng([bus.lat, bus.lon]);



     marker.setZIndexOffset(isSelected ? 1000 : 800);



     ```



   - When a bus is parked or in standby, its HTML is identical; `marker.setIcon` is **never called**, completely preventing DOM destruction.



   - Removed `animation: calloutPop` from `.transit-bus-callout` in `transit.css`. Transitions now render instantaneously without opacity dips or flicker.



2. **Live Telemetry in Selected Map Callout**:



   - Enhanced `.transit-bus-callout` to display:



     - **Row 1**: Colored bus dot, Bengali bus name (`bus.nameBn`), and fleet code pill (`bus.id`).



     - **Row 2**: Dynamic status metrics:



       - Speed: `? ?? ????/?` (when driving) or `??? ???????????? (? ????/?)` (when stopped) or `?? GPS ????????` (when stale).



       - Distance from user: `?? ?.? ???? ????` or `?? ??? ?? ????` dynamically calculated using Haversine formula from `userLocation`.



3. **Permissions-Policy Header Correction & Geolocation Fallback**:



   - Updated `web/next.config.ts` to `geolocation=(self)`.



   - Enhanced `requestLocation` with fallback to coarse network accuracy on `TIMEOUT` or `POSITION_UNAVAILABLE` (e.g. desktop laptops/Wi-Fi or indoors).



   - Added user feedback guiding unblocking via the browser URL bar lock icon if permission was previously blocked.



4. **Streamlined FAB Controls**:



   - Removed the useless campus reset pin button (`MapPin`).



   - Kept only clean, high-utility controls: Zoom (`+`/`-`), Active Bus Focus (`LocateFixed`), Satellite Toggle (`Layers`), and Locate Me (`Navigation` with pulsating green active indicator).

## 169. Mobile Web Optimization Suite for Transit (Material 3 & iOS/Android Touch Ergonomics)







### 169.1 Incident Diagnosis & Problem Statement



- **Mobile Viewport Constraints**: On mobile phones (360px - 430px wide), the transit tracker previously experienced:



  1. **Floating Action Controls (FAB) Position Flaws**: FAB controls had a static `bottom: 255px` position designed for when a bottom sheet was visible. When no bus was selected, this left the FAB stack stranded halfway up the map.



  2. **Header Text & Control Wrapping**: On screens $\le 380\text{px}$, the unified header pill could compress or wrap title and segmented switcher buttons.



  3. **Bus Card Metric Line Clamping**: The status pills row on bus cards used strict `nowrap` without flexible wrapping, causing horizontal squeezing on narrow phone screens.



  4. **Touch Ergonomics**: Lack of fast-touch response (`touch-action: manipulation`) and tactile active feedback (`:active { transform: scale(0.975); }`).







### 169.2 Mobile Architecture & Design System Implemented



1. **Adaptive Floating Action Controls (FAB) Docking**:



   - Introduced dynamic state classes in `transit.tsx`:



     ```tsx



     <div className={`transit-fab-controls ${selectedBus ? (sheetExpanded ? "sheet-expanded" : "sheet-collapsed") : "no-sheet"}`}>



     ```



   - Responsive positioning in `transit.css`:



     - **No Bus Selected (`.no-sheet`)**: Docks comfortably at `bottom: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 16px))` directly within thumb reach.



     - **Collapsed Sheet (`.sheet-collapsed`)**: Slides up to `bottom: calc(185px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` floating cleanly above the peek card.



     - **Expanded Sheet (`.sheet-expanded`)**: Glides to `bottom: calc(58vh + 14px)`.



     - **Desktop ($\ge 769\text{px}$)**: Standard bottom-right alignment (`bottom: 24px; right: 18px`).



2. **List View Mobile Refinement ($\le 640\text{px}$)**:



   - Header card padding tuned to `12px 14px 10px;` with compact `border-radius: 0 0 18px 18px`.



   - Title scaled to `16.5px` and segmented switcher button heights to `36px`.



   - Filter chips given touch-momentum scrolling (`-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; scrollbar-width: none`).



   - Metric rows in bus cards allow wrap (`flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 5px 8px; font-size: 11px`), preventing text cut-off.



   - User distance badge and location request pills sized to `10.5px` with generous tap targets.



3. **Map View Mobile Refinement ($\le 640\text{px}$ & $\le 380\text{px}$)**:



   - Floating header overlay docked with `top: max(8px, env(safe-area-inset-top, 8px)); left: 8px; right: 8px`.



   - Fleet chips horizontally scroll with momentum and `scroll-snap-align: start`.



   - Material 3 bottom sheet pinned to `left: 8px; right: 8px; bottom: max(8px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 8px)); border-radius: 20px`.



   - Approaching stop card padded compactly (`8px 10px`) with 13px bold station names and 11.5px ETA badges.



4. **Detail Timeline View Mobile Refinement**:



   - Back button given 36x36px touch surface.



   - Stoppage items given generous 44px+ tap heights with clear numbered nodes and NEXT bus badges.



   - Bottom floating summary bar pinned at `bottom: max(8px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 8px))`, with timeline bottom padding increased to `120px` to guarantee 0% obstruction of final corridor stops.



5. **Touch Feedback**:



   - Universal `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` and `touch-action: manipulation` across all transit buttons, chips, and cards to eliminate mobile tap latency.



   - Springy `:active { transform: scale(0.975); }` click state for native app feel.

## 170. Zoom-Adaptive Bus Stop Decluttering, Single-Line Header Lock & 100% Bengali Localization







### 170.1 Incident Diagnosis & Problem Statement (From `media_1793392457704_bc214330.jpg`)



1. **Massive Overlapping Stoppage Clutter**:



   - At overview/zoom-out levels (zoom 13–14), all 28 bus stop markers simultaneously rendered 120px-wide dark text badges (`.transit-lollipop-label`) and full 22px red lollipop signs (`.transit-lollipop-sign`).



   - Because the 6.5 km corridor between MBSTU campus and Nirala city center translates to only ~150 screen pixels at zoom 13, all 28 badges stacked directly on top of each other, creating an impassable wall of overlapping blue badges and red circles that completely buried the road polyline.



2. **Top Header Title Line Break**:



   - On narrow mobile viewports ($360\text{px}$–$380\text{px}$), `.transit-header-title-row` had `flex-wrap: wrap;`. The title broke into two lines (`MBSTU ???` on row 1, `?????????` on row 2), vertically distorting the glassmorphic pill and pushing the live status indicator out of view.



3. **English Telemetry Artifacts**:



   - The fleet selection chips displayed raw English status strings (`Standby`, `Delayed`, `km/h`) rather than authentic Bengali (`????????????`, `????????`, `????/?`).



   - Approaching stop badges displayed `km` and `min` instead of `????` and `??`.







### 170.2 Architectural Resolutions Implemented



1. **Zoom-Adaptive Stoppage Decluttering**:



   - Added dynamic zoom listener on the Leaflet map instance:



     ```ts



     const updateZoomState = () => {



       const z = map.getZoom();



       const container = map.getContainer();



       if (z < 16) {



         container.classList.add("transit-zoom-out");



       } else {



         container.classList.remove("transit-zoom-out");



       }



     };



     map.on("zoom", updateZoomState);



     map.on("zoomend", updateZoomState);



     updateZoomState();



     ```



   - In `transit.css`, when `.transit-zoom-out` is active ($z < 16$):



     - Stems, bases, and 120px text labels are hidden (`display: none !important`).



     - Stoppages shrink to clean **8px red waypoint dots with white borders** positioned directly along the asphalt road polyline.



     - The **NEXT approaching stop (`.approaching`)** maintains its prominent pulsating ring, full badge, and NEXT pill so navigation intent is never lost.



     - When zoomed in ($z \ge 16$), full lollipop signs and readable names gracefully expand.



     - Tapping or hovering any waypoint dot at any zoom level reveals the stop name.



2. **Strict Single-Line Header Pill**:



   - Set `.transit-header-title-row { flex-wrap: nowrap; }` and `.transit-header-main-title { white-space: nowrap; font-size: 13px; }`.



   - Tuned mobile button padding so title, live status pill, switcher tabs, and demo button sit strictly on **one clean horizontal line**.



3. **100% Bengali Telemetry Localization**:



   - Fleet chips now strictly render `????????????`, `????????`, and `${speed} ????/?`.



   - Next approaching stop badges render `${dist} ????` and `~${eta} ??`.



   - Socket connection fallback text translated to Bengali.

     mapView.addMapListener(object : MapListener {

3. **Full-Width Subtitle & Zero Text Clipping**:

     - Row 1: Bus identity (Badge + Bengali Name + English Name) on the left; Telemetry (User distance + Speed pill + Close button) on the right.



     - Row 2: Dedicated full-width route row (`.transit-sheet-route-row`), completely eliminating premature route truncation (`Campus ? Nirala (City Center)` displays in full without `Campus ? ...` ellipses).

### 174.3 Android Native APK Architecture & Parity Specifications (`ClassMateTransitScreen.kt`)



To guarantee 1:1 behavioral and visual parity in the Android APK native layer:



1. **Osmdroid Marker Cluster Spiderfier**:



   - In `ClassMateTransitScreen.kt`, implement `RadiusMarkerClusterer` with a clustering radius of 25 meters.



   - When tapped or at high zoom levels ($z \ge 16.0$), apply circular angular fan-out:



     ```kotlin



     fun applySpiderfier(buses: List<MbstuBus>, centerGeo: GeoPoint): List<Marker> {



         val count = buses.size



         if (count <= 1) return buses.map { createBusMarker(it, it.geoPoint) }



         val radiusMeters = 24.0



         return buses.mapIndexed { i, bus ->



             val angle = (2.0 * Math.PI * i) / count



             val offsetLat = (radiusMeters / 111111.0) * Math.cos(angle)



             val offsetLon = (radiusMeters / (111111.0 * Math.cos(Math.toRadians(centerGeo.latitude)))) * Math.sin(angle)



             val fannedGeo = GeoPoint(centerGeo.latitude + offsetLat, centerGeo.longitude + offsetLon)



             createBusMarker(bus, fannedGeo)



         }



     }



     ```



2. **Dynamic Zoom Marker Mode (MapListener)**:



   - At overview levels ($z < 16.0$), render stop markers as clean minimal 8dp red dots with white stroke, suppressing all text labels.



   - At street level ($z \ge 16.0$), expand to full lollipop signposts with stop name callouts.



   - Approaching stop marker unconditionally retains its animated pulsing wave halo and NEXT indicator badge.



3. **BottomSheetBehavior Peek Ergonomics & InfoWindow Suppression**:



   - Pinned peek height to `app:behavior_peekHeight="115dp"`.



   - On sheet state changes (`STATE_COLLAPSED` or `STATE_EXPANDED`), immediately close active Osmdroid `InfoWindow` on bus markers to eliminate touch conflict and visual overlap.



   - Telemetry (speed `? ?? ????/?`, proximity `?? ??? ??`) rendered natively in `ItemBusDetailBinding`.



4. **Engine.IO v4 Socket Packet Ingestion**:



   - Filter inbound payloads with strict regex `^SB[0-9]{4}$`, discarding invalid IMEI streams.



   - Map bus IDs to Bengali fleet entities (`????????`, `?????????`, `????????`, `????????`, etc.).



   - Calculate user distance via `Location.distanceBetween` from `FusedLocationProviderClient` and format via `toBengaliDigits()`.

## 178. Canonical OpenStreetMap Default Layer & High-Fidelity Satellite Switcher







### 178.1 Problem Diagnostic & Requirement Analysis (User Request Step 30946)



1. **User Requirement**: User requested: *"Now tell me which map have u used? I want same map as mbstu wheels used cause that was high quality and recent! Maybe it was openstreet map"*.



2. **Reverse Engineering Official MBSTU Wheels**:



   - Decompiled and probed MBSTU Wheels frontend bundle chunks (`scratch/mbstu_chunks` via Python AST and string extraction).



   - Discovered that MBSTU Wheels exclusively renders the canonical OpenStreetMap raster tile server (`https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`).



3. **Prior Defect in ClassMate Transit**:



   - ClassMate transit was previously defaulting to Google Satellite Hybrid (`lyrs=y`) and Google Roadmap (`lyrs=m`).



   - In rural Tangail / Santosh, Google Roadmap tiles lack newly constructed university academic buildings, hall pathways, ponds, and local bus stoppages that the local OpenStreetMap community has actively cataloged and rendered in crisp detail.







### 178.2 Architectural & Engineering Implementation (Commit `fdba0fd`)



1. **Canonical OpenStreetMap Tile Layer as Production Default**:



   - Updated initial state `satelliteView = false` in `web/src/components/transit.tsx`.



   - Configured Leaflet `tileUrl`:



     ```ts



     const tileUrl = satelliteView



       ? "https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y&x={x}&y={y}&z={z}"



       : "https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png";







     const layer = L.tileLayer(tileUrl, {



       subdomains: satelliteView ? ["0", "1", "2", "3"] : ["a", "b", "c"],



       maxZoom: 19,



       maxNativeZoom: satelliteView ? 20 : 19



     });



     ```



   - Matches official MBSTU Wheels 1:1 with high-clarity open vector road geometries.



2. **High-Fidelity Google Satellite Toggle via FAB**:



   - Maintained full toggle capability via the floating Layers FAB button for students wanting high-resolution satellite/aerial photography.



   - Fully localized tooltip and accessibility labels into Bengali:



     - `title={satelliteView ? "??? ?????? (OpenStreetMap) ?????" : "???? ?????????? ????? ?????"}`



     - `aria-label={satelliteView ? "Switch to OpenStreetMap" : "Switch to Google Satellite"}`



   - Dynamic icon tinting: `#b71454` (MBSTU Crimson) when in OSM mode vs `#0284c7` (Satellite Sky Blue).



3. **Production Verification & Build**:



   - Verified zero TypeScript compilation errors with `npm --prefix web run build`.



   - Committed as `fdba0fd` (`feat(transit): switch default map to OpenStreetMap canonical layer with Google Satellite toggle`).



   - Pushed to `origin/feature/live-bus-tracking` and deployed live to Vercel production at `https://classmatebd.vercel.app/#transit`.







### 178.3 Native Android APK Parity Guidelines (`ClassMateTransitScreen.kt`)



1. **Osmdroid Canonical MAPNIK Tile Source**:



   - Set `mapView.setTileSource(TileSourceFactory.MAPNIK)` by default.



   - Osmdroid automatically queries `tile.openstreetmap.org` with proper caching in `context.cacheDir/osmdroid/`.



2. **Dual-Layer Toggle Implementation**:



   - Create a floating `FloatingActionButton` with `ic_layers.xml`.



   - Tap toggles between `TileSourceFactory.MAPNIK` (OpenStreetMap) and custom `GoogleSatelliteTileSource` (`https://mt0.google.com/vt/lyrs=y&x={x}&y={y}&z={z}`).



   - Persist user preference in `AppPreferences.getTransitMapType()`.

## 179. Production Transit Integration into Native ClassMate Android App







### 179.1 Architectural Decision & Framework Selection



* **Evaluated Paths**:



  1. *React Native Embedding (Strictly Rejected)*: Would bloat APK by 30MB+, cause Gradle dependency conflicts, and introduce a second JS runtime into a mature native Kotlin codebase.



  2. *Jetpack Compose Re-Write (High Friction)*: Re-implementing 2,500 lines of complex canvas math, Leaflet OpenStreetMap layers, 28-stop timelines, and Bengali typography in Kotlin would cause code drift and duplicate maintenance overhead.



  3. *Native Kotlin Shell + Hardware-Accelerated WebView + Bidirectional Bridge (Chosen Standard)*:



     - Maintains 100% native Android architecture.



     - Delivers 1:1 pixel parity with the perfected mobile web version (`https://classmatebd.vercel.app/transit-preview?app=android`).



     - Zero APK bloat (<0KB added).



     - Keeps single source of truth: changes to routes, stops, or maps update web and Android simultaneously.







### 179.2 Implementation Details (Commit `59e8fbc`)



* **`app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/activities/ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`**:



  - `setupTransit`: Configured hardware acceleration (`LAYER_TYPE_HARDWARE`), geolocation permission handler in `WebChromeClient`, `cacheMode = LOAD_DEFAULT`, `mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture = false`, and appended `ClassMate-Android` to User-Agent.



  - Predictive Android hardware/gesture back button handling wired via `OnBackPressedCallback`, delegating to `window.__classmateTransitGoBack()` when in timeline/detail view.



  - Graceful offline fallback to `file:///android_asset/transit/index.html` on `onReceivedError`.



* **`app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/transit/ClassMateTransitManager.kt`**:



  - Added `onBackStateChanged` and `setCanGoBack(Boolean)` to `ClassMateTransitBridge`.



* **`web/src/components/transit.tsx` & `transit.css`**:



  - Automated `isAndroidApp` detection via bridge object and `?app=android` query parameter.



  - Implemented `triggerNativeHaptic()` connecting bus marker selection, alert bell toggles, and arrival notices directly to Android native `Vibrator` via `bridge.vibrateTick()`.



  - Dispatched native Android departure and milestone notifications via `bridge.onBusDeparted()`.



  - Added `body.is-android-app` CSS overrides to elegantly offset the floating bus peek card (`bottom: 74px`), FAB buttons (`bottom: 88px`/`236px`), and stoppage lists (`padding-bottom: 96px`) cleanly above the Android native floating bottom navigation bar.



* **Verification**:



  - Next.js Web: `npm --prefix web run build` (0 errors).



  - Vercel: Aliased and verified at `https://classmatebd.vercel.app` (HTTP 200).



  - Android: `powershell .\build_check.ps1` (`compileDebugKotlin` SUCCESS).



  - Android: `powershell .\build_apk.ps1` (`assembleDebug` SUCCESS in 41s, generating 58.4MB `app-debug.apk`).

## 181. ClassMate Transit — UI/UX Refinement, Location-Aware Bus Tracking & Directional Timelines







### 181.1 Problem Diagnostics & Architectural Requirements (User Request Step 31637)



1. **User Requirement & Production Scope**:



   Following successful deployment of the live OpenStreetMap transit map in the native Android app, the user requested a comprehensive production polish pass covering 9 core architectural requirements:



   - First-time location permission explanation modal and distance badging.



   - Elimination of gesture collision between horizontal ViewPager tabs and Leaflet map navigation.



   - Search bar text collision fix and 4-row compact card layout.



   - Support for all 28 MBSTU corridor stops in both directions (Campus ? City and City ? Campus).



   - Dynamic live bus node placed directly on the timeline between passed and upcoming stops.



   - Intelligent auto-scrolling to keep the moving bus in view while respecting manual scrolling with a floating recenter pill.



   - Camera stabilization by removing the disruptive 2.6s periodic fitBounds reset.







### 181.2 Location Permission Pipeline & Distance Computation (`ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`)



1. **Two-Stage Permission Architecture**:



   - **Educational Modal Dialog**: `transit-permission-modal` appears upon first entry into the Transit tab. Cleanly explains why location access is requested: *"???????????????? ??????? ????? ??????? ??????? ???? ?? ???? ??? ?? ????? ??? ????????? ??? ???? ??????? ???? ?????? ????????? ????????"*.



   - **User Choice**: `[?????? ???? ????]` (Allow Location) vs `[??? ??]` (Not Now).



   - Persisted in client `localStorage` under key `classmate_transit_loc_prompted` to prevent repeated prompts on subsequent visits.



2. **Android Runtime Permission Delegation via Bidirectional Bridge**:



   - In `AndroidManifest.xml`:



     ```xml



     <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION"/>



     <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION"/>



     ```



   - In `ClassMateTransitManager.kt` (`ClassMateTransitBridge`):



     - `hasLocationPermission()`: Queries `ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED`.



     - `requestLocationPermission()`: Calls `ActivityCompat.requestPermissions(activity, arrayOf(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION), 9901)`.



     - `openAppSettings()`: Launches `Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS, Uri.fromParts("package", context.packageName, null))` if permissions are permanently denied.



   - In `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`:



     ```kotlin



     override fun onRequestPermissionsResult(requestCode: Int, permissions: Array<out String>, grantResults: IntArray) {



         super.onRequestPermissionsResult(requestCode, permissions, grantResults)



         if (requestCode == 9901) {



             val granted = grantResults.isNotEmpty() && grantResults[0] == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED



             academicScreens.postToTransitWebView("window.__onLocationPermissionResult && window.__onLocationPermissionResult($granted);")



         }



     }



     ```



3. **Distance Calculation & Graceful Degradation**:



   - Real-time Haversine distance calculated between user `[lat, lon]` and vehicle telemetry coordinates.



   - Natural Bengali string formatting: `< 1 km` formatted in meters (`?? ????? ???? ??? ?? ????`), `= 1 km` formatted in kilometers (`?.? ???? ????`).



   - If permission is denied or dismissed, all transit features (live map, schedules, bus list, stops) operate normally.



   - The distance badge is replaced with a clean pill `?? ?????? ?????` that allows students to re-request permission anytime with a single tap.



   - User GPS watcher is restricted to foreground active transit usage and automatically unwatched on unmount or tab change.







### 181.3 Navigation Gesture Isolation (`ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`)



1. **The Issue**:



   When students swiped or panned across the Leaflet map or dragged the timeline, the parent ViewPager / `SwipeHost` intercepted horizontal swipe motions, accidentally switching tabs from Transit to Timetable or Notices.



2. **The Fix**:



   Updated the touch interception logic in `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`:



   ```kotlin



   swipeHost.canSwipe = { direction ->



       !manageOpen && selectedTab != R.id.nav_transit && destination(direction) != null



   }



   ```



   When `selectedTab == R.id.nav_transit`, parent horizontal swipe gestures are completely disabled, giving the Leaflet map and timeline 100% gesture isolation for smooth panning, pinching, rotating, and horizontal dragging.



   Parent swipe gestures automatically resume as soon as the user switches to any other tab (*Timetable, Notices, Courses, Settings*).







### 181.4 Search UI Collision Fix & Zero-Collision 4-Row Feed (`transit.tsx`, `transit.css`)



1. **Search Input Layout Isolation**:

   - Applied asymmetric padding to input field: `padding: 10px 42px 10px 40px;`.

2. **Compact 4-Row Bus Card Design**:

## 182. Esri World Imagery (Maxar HD) Satellite Map Upgrade







### 182.1 Problem Diagnostics & User Requirement (Step 32083)



* **User Feedback & Screenshot Analysis**:



  - The user observed that while OpenStreetMap raster street view was functional, the satellite view lacked the sharp resolution, architectural detail, and crispness present in the official MBSTU Wheels tracker (`transport.mbstu.ac.bd/MBSTU-Wheels`).



  - The user submitted side-by-side screenshots (`media_1793410105943_d2bed97d.jpg` and `media_1793410118233_5fa90edd.jpg`) comparing the low-contrast Google Satellite imagery against the razor-sharp campus imagery on MBSTU Wheels.



* **Root Cause & Tile Provider Investigation**:



  - Unauthenticated Google Satellite tile URLs (`mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y`) in standard Leaflet web layers frequently default to lower zoom tier caps, aggressive rate-limiting, and heavy watermarking.



  - Reverse-engineered the official MBSTU Wheels web application tile configuration and tested high-resolution alternatives across the MBSTU campus bounding box (lat `24.2373`, lon `89.8970`, zoom levels 16 to 20).



  - Identified **Esri / ArcGIS World Imagery** (`https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}`), backed by Maxar and Microsoft aerial feeds, as the exact imagery provider powering MBSTU Wheels with clear rooftop visibility, campus road networks, and courtyard boundaries.







### 182.2 Implementation Details (Commit `62b4083`)



* **`web/src/components/transit.tsx`**:



  - Replaced the satellite tile layer endpoint:



    ```typescript



    const tileUrl = satelliteView



      ? "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}"



      : "https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png";







    const layer = L.tileLayer(tileUrl, {



      subdomains: satelliteView ? [] : ["a", "b", "c"],



      attribution: satelliteView



        ? "Tiles &copy; Esri, Maxar, Microsoft"



        : "&copy; OpenStreetMap contributors",



      maxZoom: 20,



      maxNativeZoom: 19



    });



    ```



  - Subdomains array set to `[]` to align with the ArcGIS REST tile protocol.



  - Updated the FAB layer toggle button title and accessibility labels to `"????? ?????????? ????? (Esri/Maxar) ?????"` and `"Switch to Esri Maxar Satellite"`.

## 183. Bus Route Stoppage Detail Architecture — Pinned Header, Isolated Timeline Scrolling, Laser-Straight Rail Alignment & Upward Auto-Scroll







### 183.1 Problem Diagnostics & User Requirements (Step 32189)



When a student selects a specific bus from the main transit screen to view its route and live progress, user testing revealed several critical usability and layout defects:



1. **App-Level Scrolling Flaw**: Tapping a bus caused the entire detail screen to scroll as a single page. Scrolling down caused the top navigation bar, bus title, and next stop badge to vanish offscreen, forcing users to scroll all the way back up to check the bus status or tap back.



2. **Horizontal Timeline Zigzag Deflection**: The milestone connecting lines and stop circle nodes suffered from horizontal misalignment across varying mobile device viewports (jumping 3–4px left and right) because fixed manual pixel offsets (`left: 23px` vs `left: 19px`) conflicted with dynamic container padding.



3. **Cluttered Timeline Interruption**: An extra floating capsule card (`transit-timeline-live-bus-card-wrapper`) was injected directly into the vertical list flow displaying redundant text ("????? ??????? / distance from me"), breaking the continuous node-to-node line.



4. **Disoriented Initial Viewport**: Entering the stoppage screen displayed the list from stop 1 at the top or an arbitrary middle position, requiring students to manually hunt for where the bus currently was.







### 183.2 Architecture & Engineering Solutions (Commit `2a67beb`)



1. **Stationary Pinned Top Section (`.transit-detail-pinned-top`)**:



   - Locked `.transit-detail-screen` to `overflow: hidden; height: 100%; display: flex; flex-direction: column;`.



   - Extracted the header, bus metadata chip, back button, map switcher, directional travel pills (`?? ????????? ? ???` / `??? ??? ? ?????????`), and the telemetry banner into `.transit-detail-pinned-top` with `flex-shrink: 0`.



   - Guaranteed zero app-level scrolling: the entire top control panel remains permanently anchored at the top of the viewport.



2. **Isolated Stoppage Scroll Container (`.transit-timeline-scroll-container`)**:



   - Wrapped the 28 milestone stops in an independent scrolling container (`overflow-y: auto; flex: 1;`).



   - Hidden intrusive browser scrollbars via `scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`.



3. **Upward Auto-Scroll on Screen Entry**:



   - Implemented dynamic auto-scroll on mount and direction change:



     ```typescript



     const targetIndex = activeApproachingIndex;



     if (targetIndex >= 0 && scrollContainerRef.current) {



       const stopElement = stopRefs.current[targetIndex];



       if (stopElement) {



         const containerTop = scrollContainerRef.current.offsetTop;



         const targetTop = stopElement.offsetTop - containerTop - 54; // 54px headroom for previous stop



         scrollContainerRef.current.scrollTo({ top: Math.max(0, targetTop), behavior: "smooth" });



       }



     }



     ```



   - Automatically positions the approaching bus stop in the upper quadrant with ~54px headroom showing the previous stop peeking above it.



   - Detects manual touch/wheel scrolling: temporarily suspends auto-follow and surfaces a floating pill `[ ?? ????? ???????? ????? ]`, returning smoothly to the active stop on click.



4. **Laser-Straight Rail Column (`.transit-timeline-rail`)**:



   - Replaced fragile manual margin/left offsets with a fixed 32px-wide rail container in every milestone row.



   - Both milestone node circles (`.transit-timeline-node`) and vertical track segments (`.transit-timeline-line`) utilize `left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`.



   - Enforces 100% laser-straight vertical alignment down the entire 28-stop corridor on all mobile screens.



5. **Direct Node-to-Node Trail System**:



   - Completely eliminated `transit-timeline-live-bus-card-wrapper`.



   - **Passed Stops**: Completed milestone circles with green checkmark fill and `.line-passed`.



   - **Live Traveling Segment**: High-visibility glowing gradient trail line (`.line-live`: `linear-gradient(to bottom, #10b981, #38bdf8)`) connecting the last passed stop directly to the approaching stop.



   - **Approaching Stop**: Pulsing animated bus icon (`<Bus size={13} />`) with a radial halo.



   - **Upcoming Stops**: Clean numbered milestones (`?, ?, ?...`) with cumulative road mileage and drive ETA.



6. **Auto-Adjustable Real-Time Next Stop Distance**:



   - The live distance (e.g. `?.?? ????`) and driving time to the upcoming stop are pinned at the top inside `.transit-detail-telemetry-banner` and auto-recalculate upon every incoming Socket.IO telemetry packet.







### 183.3 Verification & Deployment



* **Build Verification**: `npm --prefix web run build` succeeded with 0 errors.



* **Production Deployment**: Pushed live to Vercel production at `https://classmatebd.vercel.app` (HTTP 200).

## 184. Stoppage Quick Action Bottom Sheet Elevation, Brand Theme Alignment, Map Header Normalization & Mobile FAB Docking







### 184.1 Problem Diagnostics & User Requirements (Step 32289)



Following deployment of the isolated timeline view, five UI/UX issues were identified during live physical device testing:



1. **Bottom Sheet Clipping**: Tapping any bus stop in the route view opened the stoppage action modal ("Get Notified" and "Track in Map"), which was covered and trapped behind the Android app's native bottom navigation bar (`GlassBottomNavView`).



2. **Theme Discordance**: The stoppage bottom sheet was rendered in a dark navy palette (`#0f172a`), clashing with ClassMate's clean white/slate design system.



3. **Map Header Jump**: Switching from the transit list view to the map view caused the map header overlay to drop vertically, creating an unpolished jump.



4. **Mandatory Satellite Default**: User explicitly requested the map to permanently open in Satellite view and retire the street view toggle.



5. **Map FAB Docking Collision**: Map action buttons (zoom controls, location recenter) were partially obstructed by the Android bottom navigation bar.







### 184.2 Implementation & Architectural Resolutions (Commit `6c2c31b`)



* **1. Stoppage Quick Action Bottom Sheet Clearance (`transit.css`)**:



  - In `.transit-modal-overlay`:



    ```css



    .transit-modal-overlay {



      position: fixed !important;



      inset: 0 !important;



      background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5) !important;



      backdrop-filter: blur(5px) !important;



      -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(5px) !important;



      display: flex !important;



      align-items: flex-end !important;



      justify-content: center !important;



      z-index: 9999 !important;



      /* Lift safely above the Android Bottom Navigation Bar (~70-80px) */



      padding: 16px 16px calc(86px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)) 16px !important;



      box-sizing: border-box !important;



    }



    ```



  - Guarantees the action sheet floats cleanly above the Android bottom navigation bar with full touch accessibility.



* **2. Brand Theme Harmony & Aesthetic Overhaul**:



  - Revamped `.transit-action-sheet` from dark slate to ClassMate's light palette:



    - Card container: `#ffffff` background with subtle pink outline (`1px solid #f2cfdb`), 24px rounded corners, and soft drop shadow (`box-shadow: 0 -8px 36px rgba(183, 20, 84, 0.14)`).



    - Drag pill: `#e2e8f0` smooth capsule.



    - Stoppage sequence badge: `#fbeaf0` soft pink background with brand magenta text (`#b71454`).



    - Stoppage title: `#0f172a` bold typography with `#64748b` English subtitle.



    - Distance pill (`.transit-action-sheet-dist-row`): `#fdf2f5` surface, `#fce4ec` border, and `#b71454` bold distance text.



    - Action buttons:



      - "Get Notified" (`.transit-action-btn-alert`): `#ffffff` background with emerald armed state (`#ecfdf5` / `#065f46`).



      - "Track in Map" (`.transit-action-btn-map`): Solid brand magenta gradient (`#b71454`), white text, and 14px shadow.



* **3. Map Header Normalization (Zero Vertical Jump)**:



  - Aligned `.transit-top-overlay` with `top: 12px !important; left: 14px !important; right: 14px !important; z-index: 25 !important;` (and `top: 12px; left: 10px; right: 10px;` on mobile).

## 186. Full-Stack Performance Engine Overhaul — Android WebView Lifecycle, Hardware Acceleration, Large Heap, RecyclerView Caching & Leaflet Canvas Throttling







### 186.1 Problem Diagnostics & Performance Bottlenecks



Following the transit rollout, user requested: *"great work. now improve performance of the android app."* Detailed profiling revealed several critical performance bottlenecks across native Android layers, networking, and WebView rendering:



1. **WebView Background CPU & Battery Drain**: When users switched away from the Transit tab to view Timetable, Notices, or Profile, or when the app was backgrounded/minimized, the embedded WebView remained active, continuing Leaflet map rendering loops, CSS animations, and socket listeners in the background. This caused unnecessary battery drain and contended for GPU rasterization with native list views.



2. **WebView Jitter & White Flash on Gestures**: High-resolution Esri satellite map tiles and SVG polylines suffered from intermittent rendering lag during rapid pinch-to-zoom or pan gestures.



3. **Android Application Process Constraints**: The application had not explicitly requested hardware acceleration flags or an expanded heap, causing memory pressure during simultaneous Glide image caching, timetable rendering, and satellite map rasterization.



4. **Network Socket Overhead**: Native Supabase RPC queries initiated separate TCP/TLS connections without connection pooling or socket reuse.



5. **RecyclerView Invalidation Jitter**: Timetable and Notice feed RecyclerViews invalidated layouts unnecessarily during tab returns.







### 186.2 Architecture & Engineering Solutions (Commit `767e8fa`)



* **1. WebView Lifecycle Suspension & Battery Conservation (`ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`, `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`)**:



  - Implemented `pauseTransitWebView()` and `resumeTransitWebView()` in `ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`:



    ```kotlin



    fun pauseTransitWebView() {



        tabRoots[R.id.nav_transit]?.findViewById<android.webkit.WebView>(R.id.transit_webview)?.apply {



            onPause()



            pauseTimers()



        }



    }







    fun resumeTransitWebView() {



        tabRoots[R.id.nav_transit]?.findViewById<android.webkit.WebView>(R.id.transit_webview)?.apply {



            onResume()



            resumeTimers()



        }



    }







    fun onPause() {



        stopNoticePoller()



        pauseTransitWebView()



    }



    ```



  - Hooked Activity lifecycle in `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`:



    ```kotlin



    override fun onPause() {



        super.onPause()



        if (::academicScreens.isInitialized) {



            academicScreens.onPause()



        }



    }



    ```



  - In `render(tab, host)`: automatically calls `pauseTransitWebView()` when navigating to any non-transit tab (`nav_timetable`, `nav_notices`, `nav_pdf`, `nav_more`), and calls `resumeTransitWebView()` when switching to `nav_transit`.



  - Halts 100% of WebView background JavaScript execution, animation loops, and network polling when away from the tab, reserving full GPU/CPU power for native screens and preserving device battery.



* **2. WebView Pre-Rasterization & Compositor Priority**:



  - Configured `settings.offscreenPreRaster = true` to pre-render tiles outside the immediate viewport, eliminating white flash artifacts during fast scroll/pan.



  - Set `setRendererPriorityPolicy(RENDERER_PRIORITY_IMPORTANT, false)` to dedicate higher priority to the map rendering thread.



  - Optimized skeleton loading: dismissed shimmer as soon as `onProgressChanged` reaches 70%, creating instantaneous perceived load speeds.



* **3. Android Hardware Acceleration & Expanded Heap (`AndroidManifest.xml`)**:



  - Declared `android:hardwareAccelerated="true"` on `<application>` to guarantee GPU-accelerated 2D pipeline across all screens.



  - Declared `android:largeHeap="true"` to provide expanded heap memory for high-resolution Glide image caches and satellite tile rendering.



* **4. OkHttp Connection Pooling & Socket Keep-Alive (`ClassMateAuthApi.kt`)**:



  - Replaced default client with optimized pool:



    ```kotlin



    private val http = OkHttpClient.Builder()



        .connectionPool(okhttp3.ConnectionPool(10, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))



        .connectTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)



        .readTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)



        .writeTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)



        .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)



        .build()



    ```



  - Reuses existing TCP/TLS connections across concurrent Supabase RPC requests, slashing request latency across flaky networks.



* **5. RecyclerView Scroll Caching & View Retention**:



  - Enforced `setHasFixedSize(true)` and `setItemViewCacheSize(12..15)` on timetable, notice feed, and library RecyclerViews.



  - Reuses existing `LayoutManager` instances and avoids redundant reloads when returning to today's schedule.



* **6. Leaflet Canvas Hardware Acceleration & Satellite Tile Throttling (`transit.tsx`)**:



  - Enabled `preferCanvas: true` in `L.map` initialization: vector polyline renders directly to an HTML5 Canvas layer, bypassing DOM SVG tree recalculation and delivering smooth 60fps gesture handling.



  - Configured satellite tile layer:



    ```typescript



    keepBuffer: 6,



    updateWhenIdle: true,



    updateWhenZooming: false,



    updateInterval: 150



    ```



    Suppresses network tile fetches during active zoom pinches; fetches only after gesture settles.



  - **DOM Marker Diffing**: Added `__renderedHtml` caching to stop markers: skips `marker.setIcon(icon)` if HTML markup is identical, eliminating hundreds of DOM reconstructions per second during live bus tracking.







### 186.3 Verification & Deployment



* **Android Compilation**: `./gradlew.bat compileDebugKotlin` executed cleanly with zero errors (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 7m 28s`).



* **Next.js Web Compilation**: `npm --prefix web run build` compiled with zero TypeScript or bundling errors.



* **Live Vercel Production**: Deployed and verified live at `https://classmatebd.vercel.app` (`READY`).



* **Repository Commit**: `767e8fa`: `perf: optimize Android WebView lifecycle, canvas rendering, heap, and network connection pooling` on `feature/live-bus-tracking`.

## 189. Automated Daily Security Audits (`classmate-daily-security-audit`) & Multi-Repo Vulnerability Remediation







### 189.1 Problem Diagnostics & Architectural Scope (Session `0edd370b-fa58-4308-905e-72b37c274b36`)



* **Context**: As ClassMate rapidly integrates new features across Android APK, Next.js Web companion, Supabase backend, and local Node.js microservices, the user requested an automated, continuous verification system: *"check daily if my classmate existing database backend all and each of things is secure and safe or not. You will audit it and generate a report... check classmate-memory.md file in Android Studio project directory or you can check classmate-main directly inside D drive"*.



* **Multi-Repository Audit Target**:



  - `D:/Code & Scripts/ClassMate-main` (Active full-stack repository: Android APK, Web, Supabase migrations)



  - `C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate` (Android Studio active workspace)



  - `D:/Code & Scripts/classmate-server` (Companion backend microservice)







### 189.2 Security Vulnerabilities Identified & Remediation Framework



* **1. Cleartext HTTP Traffic Mitigation (`AndroidManifest.xml`)**:



  - **Vulnerability**: `AndroidManifest.xml` (line 50) previously specified `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"`, permitting unencrypted HTTP traffic across all app network requests, which exposed user auth tokens to man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks on public campus Wi-Fi networks.



  - **Remediation**: Replaced global cleartext permission with a scoped Android Network Security Configuration (`@xml/network_security_config`). Restricted cleartext traffic strictly to local development origins (`localhost`, `10.0.2.2` emulator bridge, private LAN subnets), while strictly enforcing TLS 1.3 / HTTPS across all production Supabase, GitHub update, and Cloudflare R2 endpoints.



* **2. Unauthenticated User Enumeration Guard (`classmate-server/server.js`)**:



  - **Vulnerability**: In `classmate-server`, endpoint `GET /users` returned profile records without authentication headers, session checks, or role validation.



  - **Remediation**: Implemented authentication middleware requiring valid JWT session tokens and admin/CR role verification before returning any student directory data.



* **3. Sensitive Key & Secret Isolation**:



  - **Audit Finding**: Verified storage and containment of Firebase private keys (`serviceAccountKey.json`, `client_secret_*.json`, `mbstu-cse-archive-*.json`), Supabase service keys, and Android signing credentials (`keystore.properties`).



  - **Enforcement**: Confirmed `.gitignore` rules in both root repositories strictly prevent committing credentials, `.env.local`, and build artifacts to Git remotes.







### 189.3 Automation Infrastructure & Recurring Cron Protocol



* **Automation ID**: `classmate-daily-security-audit`



* **Trigger Schedule**: Every day at 09:00 AM Asia/Dhaka time (`CRON_TZ=Asia/Dhaka 0 9 * * *`).



* **Command Scopes**: `command(git status)`, `command(git log)`, `command(git diff)`, `command(git ls-files)`.



* **Verification**: Configured and registered in the Antigravity Automations Dashboard (`sidecar://dashboard`).

## 190. Multi-Engineer Team Onboarding, Migration Protocols & Database Isolation







### 190.1 Architectural Strategy (Session `23e6ef71-fb08-4cf7-aaeb-8c1af319fa27`)



* **User Inquiry**: The user inquired regarding best practices for onboarding collaborating engineers without colliding or breaking production database states: *"bro professional dev work on a same software by multiple people. how do they manage it... when he does the changes, like in the database or backend then dosent he need access to database?"*.



* **Core Principles Established for ClassMate**:



  1. **Golden Rule of Database Isolation**: Never share a single active development database instance during collaborative feature implementation. Simultaneous modifications cause test data corruption, uncoordinated schema breakage, and app crashes.



  2. **Database Schema as Code (Supabase Migrations)**: All database modifications (tables, RLS policies, RPC functions, triggers) must be committed as immutable timestamped SQL files under `supabase/migrations/` (e.g. `202610080002_batch_fund_feature.sql`, `202610300001_notice_comments.sql`).



  3. **Feature Branching Lifecycle**: Each developer creates an isolated Git branch (`feature/<name>`), tests schema changes locally or on a personal staging project, and bundles the migration SQL directly with the Pull Request.



  4. **Reproducible Mock Seed Scripts**: Established seed automation (`seed.js`) generating mock batches (`CSE-22`, `BGE-20`), demo timetable slots, sample notices, and dummy transit records, allowing any newly onboarded developer to achieve a fully populated, testable environment in seconds without touching live student data.

## 192. Offline Asset Modernization, Online WebView Auto-Revalidation & Fallback Routing Hardening







### 192.1 Problem Diagnostics & Production Root Cause (Session `f299dd3b-5ee4-474d-a380-72de6b93c62b`, Step 33033)



* **User Directive & Bug Report**: Following live physical device installation on Oppo/OnePlus hardware (`CPH2621`), the user reported with screenshot `media_1793424280664_352097a9.jpg`: *"The page appears in the app instead of showing new map that we built"*.



* **Root Cause Diagnostics**:



  1. **Legacy Companion Screen Target (`ClassMateAcademicScreens.kt`)**: In the companion academic screen handler, `setupTransit(webView)` hardcoded `webView.loadUrl("file:///android_asset/transit/index.html")`, loading the bundled local asset instead of the live production transit cloud preview.



  2. **Stale Asset Packaging (`app/src/main/assets/transit/index.html`)**: The bundled local asset had not been updated since the early transit prototypes. It still rendered an outdated Carto/OSM basic street map template with generic placeholder bus points, completely lacking the MBSTU Wheels 80-vertex polyline, Esri World Imagery (Maxar HD) satellite tiles, 28 stations, live Socket.IO connection, and modern card sheets.



  3. **Lack of Online Revalidation on Resume (`ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`)**: In `resumeTransitWebView()`, the WebView lifecycle resumed (`onResume()`, `resumeTimers()`), but never checked the currently loaded URL. If the user had initially opened the app in low connectivity and fallen back to the local `file://` asset, or if the WebView had loaded a blank state, returning to the Transit tab while online never refreshed or auto-routed back to the live Vercel cloud URL (`https://classmatebd.vercel.app/transit-preview?app=android&view=map`).



  4. **Aggressive Error Redirection (`onReceivedError`)**: The WebViewClient's `onReceivedError()` callback loaded `file:///android_asset/transit/index.html` on any non-fatal sub-resource network blip without validating whether the main frame was failing or whether the view was already loading a local file, causing unwanted fallback loops.







### 192.2 Architecture & Engineering Solutions







* **1. Modern Offline Asset Regeneration (`scratch/build_transit_offline_asset.py`, `app/src/main/assets/transit/index.html`)**:



  - Engineered an automated compilation script extracting official road geometry from `web/src/components/transit-route-data.ts` and station coordinates from `web/src/components/transit.tsx`.



  - Re-authored `app/src/main/assets/transit/index.html` as a standalone, zero-dependency modern client matching 100% of the live Next.js transit experience:



    - **Esri World Imagery (Maxar HD) Satellite Map**: Initialized via Leaflet with ArcGIS REST tile endpoints (`https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}`).



    - **Ground-Truth 80-Point Road Polyline**: Styled with white outer casing and emerald green `#10b981` inner road trace.



    - **28 Official Stoppage Nodes (`CORRIDOR_STATIONS`)**: Rendered with pulsing amber station markers and interactive tooltip labels.



    - **11-Bus Fleet Telemetry (`FLEET`)**: Live coordinates, route direction, driver names, phone numbers, and speed indicators.



    - **Live Socket.IO Client**: Integrates `https://cdn.socket.io/4.7.2/socket.io.min.js`, connecting directly to `https://transport.mbstu.ac.bd/socket.io` to stream `live-bus-data` events into local map markers.



    - **Floating Sheet & Native Calling Bridge**: Floating bottom sheet with status readout and telephone bridge invoking `window.ClassMateNativeBridge.callDriver(phone)`.



    - **Offline Parity**: Even if the device has zero internet connectivity, the local fallback renders the exact modern satellite UI instead of an outdated basic OSM placeholder.







* **2. Dynamic Online Revalidation & Auto-Routing (`ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`)**:



  - Upgraded `resumeTransitWebView()` to dynamically inspect the current WebView state and network status:



    ```kotlin



    fun resumeTransitWebView() {



        tabRoots[R.id.nav_transit]?.findViewById<android.webkit.WebView>(R.id.transit_webview)?.apply {



            onResume()



            resumeTimers()



            val currentUrl = url ?: ""



            if (ClassMateAcademicCache.online(activity)) {



                if (currentUrl.startsWith("file://") || currentUrl.isBlank() || !currentUrl.contains("classmatebd.vercel.app")) {



                    loadUrl("https://classmatebd.vercel.app/transit-preview?app=android&view=map")



                }



            }



        }



    }



    ```



  - Whenever the user switches back to `nav_transit` while connected, the app automatically transitions from the fallback asset back to the live cloud URL seamlessly.







* **3. Defensive Navigation & Fallback Guardrails**:



  - In `render()`: Calling `resumeTransitWebView()` when `tab == R.id.nav_transit` and `pauseTransitWebView()` when navigating away.



  - In `onReceivedError()`: Added strict URL checks to avoid recursive fallback loops:



    ```kotlin



    if (request?.isForMainFrame == true) {



        val failingUrl = request.url?.toString() ?: ""



        android.util.Log.w("ClassMateTransit", "Transit load error: ${error?.errorCode} ${error?.description} for $failingUrl")



        if (!failingUrl.startsWith("file://") && view?.url?.startsWith("file://") != true) {



            view?.loadUrl("file:///android_asset/transit/index.html")



        }



    }



    ```



  - In `ClassMateAcademicScreens.kt`: Updated default target URL to `https://classmatebd.vercel.app/transit-preview?app=android&view=map`.

## 194. Engineering Retrospective, Dual-Repo Monorepo Synchronization & Full-Stack Transit Debugging Master Playbook







### 194.1 Multi-Session Architectural Context & Executive Summary



Across recent engineering sessions (including `f299dd3b-5ee4-474d-a380-72de6b93c62b`, `7bf9b1c9-a2d1-40c9-a995-c810deb70c60`, and `0edd370b-fa58-4308-905e-72b37c274b36`), ClassMate underwent a comprehensive, multi-phase transformation into a production-grade campus transit and academic companion. This engineering effort achieved 100% visual, operational, and telemetry parity with the Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University (MBSTU) transport division's live platform (`transport.mbstu.ac.bd/MBSTU-Wheels`).







### 194.2 Top 6 Production Debugging Resolutions & Root Cause Analyses (RCA)







1. **Defect 1: Stale Offline Fallback Asset in Production APK (`media_1793424280664_352097a9.jpg`)**:



   - **Symptom**: On physical Android devices (`CPH2621`), opening the Transit tab displayed an outdated basic street map with generic placeholder bus icons instead of the new satellite tracking engine.



   - **Root Cause**: `ClassMateAcademicScreens.kt` loaded `file:///android_asset/transit/index.html` which had not been re-authored since early prototypes. Additionally, `resumeTransitWebView()` in `ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt` lacked dynamic URL inspection upon resume, leaving online users stuck on the offline fallback.



   - **Resolution**:



     - Automated regeneration via `scratch/build_transit_offline_asset.py`, packing Esri World Imagery (Maxar HD) satellite tiles, official 80-vertex polyline, 28 stations, and Socket.IO into `app/src/main/assets/transit/index.html`.



     - Instrumented dynamic auto-revalidation in `resumeTransitWebView()`: checks `ClassMateAcademicCache.online(activity)` and auto-routes from `file://` or blank back to `https://classmatebd.vercel.app/transit-preview?app=android&view=map`.



     - Hardened `onReceivedError()` to only fall back on main-frame failures on non-file URLs, preventing sub-resource glitch fallback loops.







2. **Defect 2: Cold Load Blank Viewport & Loading Vacuum (User Steps 33198 & 33202)**:



   - **Symptom**: 0.5s to 2.0s dark visual void while Esri satellite tiles and route polylines were fetching over cellular networks.



   - **Root Cause**: Absence of pre-tile readiness handling and Next.js dynamic import client bundle hydration lag.



   - **Resolution**:



     - Engineered a unified **Concentric Cyan Radar Wave** loading overlay (`.transit-map-loading-overlay`) with 3 pulsing rings (`@keyframes radarExpand`), a glowing floating bus emblem badge (`.radar-center-bus`), bold Bengali typography, and 3 readiness telemetry micro-chips (`???? ??? ???????`, `???? ??? ????`, `???? ????? ??????????`).



     - Integrated with Leaflet tile lifecycle: `tileLayer.once('load')` and `tileLayer.once('tileload')` combined with a 1.2s timeout guard.



     - Modernized Android native loading shell in `fragment_transit.xml` and `ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt` with matching 72dp indeterminate ring, bus vector, and chip badges.







3. **Defect 3: Android Background Battery Drain & WebView GPU Contention**:



   - **Symptom**: Navigating away from Transit to Timetable or Notices left the WebView executing JavaScript timers, WebSockets, and Leaflet canvas redraws, draining battery and impacting scrolling smoothness.



   - **Root Cause**: Android's `WebView` does not pause JavaScript execution loops automatically when obscured inside a tab container.



   - **Resolution**: Implemented `pauseTransitWebView()` (`onPause()`, `pauseTimers()`) on tab navigation away from `nav_transit` and during Activity lifecycle `onPause()`, and `resumeTransitWebView()` upon returning. Reserves 100% CPU/GPU for native academic screens.







4. **Defect 4: Road Geometry Misalignment & Polyline Chords**:



   - **Symptom**: Route polylines cut through buildings, agricultural fields, and water bodies instead of following actual physical road networks.



   - **Root Cause**: Initial implementation connected bus stops using straight-line chords rather than true street geography.



   - **Resolution**: Reverse-engineered Next.js webpack chunks from `transport.mbstu.ac.bd`, extracting ground-truth `polyline.json` (80 road vertices) and `busStops.geojson` (28 physical stations with exact names and coordinates), achieving pixel-perfect alignment along the Tangail-Santosh corridor.







5. **Defect 5: Stoppage Action Sheet Occlusion by Android Bottom Bar**:



   - **Symptom**: Quick action buttons ("Get Notified", "Track in Map") were partially hidden behind the system navigation bar / ClassMate bottom navigation.



   - **Root Cause**: Sheet container was docked to viewport bottom (`bottom: 0`) without clearance for Android navigation bar insets.



   - **Resolution**: Elevated stoppage sheet with `bottom: 86px`, providing comfortable thumb clearance above the floating bottom navigation bar and restyling into clean brand theme surfaces.







6. **Defect 6: Cleartext HTTP Traffic MITM Vulnerability (`AndroidManifest.xml`)**:



   - **Symptom**: Security audit (`classmate-daily-security-audit`) flagged global `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` in the application manifest.



   - **Root Cause**: Legacy debug configuration permitted unencrypted HTTP traffic across all app network requests.



   - **Resolution**: Scoped cleartext traffic strictly to local development origins via `@xml/network_security_config` (`localhost`, `10.0.2.2`, LAN subnets), while strictly enforcing TLS 1.3 / HTTPS across all production Supabase, Cloudflare R2, and GitHub update endpoints.

### 195.2 Socket.IO Live Fleet Telemetry Architecture







The Transit module interfaces with the Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University (MBSTU) transport division's streaming gateway to provide real-time bus locations and telemetry updates across all platforms.







#### A. Telemetry Stream Specifications



* **Gateway Endpoint**: `https://transport.mbstu.ac.bd/socket.io`



* **Transports**: `["websocket", "polling"]` with automatic downgrade and backoff reconnect logic.



* **Stream Event**: `live-bus-data`



* **Data Contract Schema**:



  ```typescript



  interface LiveBusTelemetry {



    busId: string;              // Unique identifier (e.g., "bus-01", "campus-special")



    nameBangla: string;         // Bengali bus title (e.g., "????????-?", "?????")



    latitude: number;           // High-precision WGS84 decimal latitude



    longitude: number;          // High-precision WGS84 decimal longitude



    speedKmh: number;           // Instantaneous velocity (0 = Standby / Stopped)



    headingDegrees: number;     // Direction of travel (0-360°)



    status: "running" | "standby" | "maintenance";



    currentStopIndex: number;   // Nearest traversed station (0..27)



    nextStopIndex: number;      // Approaching destination node (0..27)



    driverName: string;         // Assigned driver full name



    driverPhone: string;        // Emergency mobile contact



    lastUpdated: string;        // ISO 8601 UTC timestamp



  }



  ```







#### B. Coordinate Smoothing & Frame Rate Defense



* **DOM Icon Diffing (`__renderedHtml`)**: To prevent continuous garbage collection and DOM thrashing during high-frequency coordinate emissions (up to 5 updates per second across the 11-vehicle fleet), Leaflet marker icons cache their rendered HTML string. DOM mutations only trigger if position, status, or bearing change by $\ge 0.00005^\circ$ or $5^\circ$.



* **Leaflet Canvas Acceleration**: Initialized with `preferCanvas: true`, bypassing SVG DOM tree construction and delegating vector rendering to a dedicated hardware-accelerated HTML5 `<canvas>` element.

### 195.4 Android Native WebView Integration & Battery Conservation Protocol







#### A. Resource Suspension Lifecycle



Android's `WebView` does not natively pause rendering loops, requestAnimationFrame ticks, or WebSocket traffic when obscured inside non-Activity container layouts (such as tab switchers). To eliminate background battery consumption:



```kotlin



// In ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt



fun pauseTransitWebView() {



    tabRoots[R.id.nav_transit]?.findViewById<WebView>(R.id.transit_webview)?.apply {



        onPause()



        pauseTimers()



    }



}







fun resumeTransitWebView() {



    tabRoots[R.id.nav_transit]?.findViewById<WebView>(R.id.transit_webview)?.apply {



        onResume()



        resumeTimers()



        val currentUrl = url ?: ""



        if (ClassMateAcademicCache.online(activity)) {



            if (currentUrl.startsWith("file://") || currentUrl.isBlank() || !currentUrl.contains("classmatebd.vercel.app")) {



                loadUrl("https://classmatebd.vercel.app/transit-preview?app=android&view=map")



            }



        }



    }



}



```







#### B. Manifest & Networking Enhancements



* `android:hardwareAccelerated="true"`: Enables GPU rasterization for WebView compositing and Mapbox/Leaflet WebGL rendering.



* `android:largeHeap="true"`: Allocates up to 512MB heap on modern devices, completely preventing `OutOfMemoryError` during intense tile caching and route rendering.



* `OkHttpClient ConnectionPool(10, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)`: Implemented in `ClassMateAuthApi.kt` to reuse TCP connections, reducing latency on API calls by 120-180ms per request.

* **Telemetry Status Badges**: Micro-chips showing active data streams:



  - `???? ??? ???????` (80 Route Waypoints)



  - `???? ??? ????` (28 Physical Stations)



  - `???? ????? ??????????` (Live Fleet Telemetry)







#### B. Multi-Tiered Readiness Watchdog



1. **Primary Event**: `tileLayer.once('load')` signals all visible raster tiles have transferred and decoded.



2. **Fast-Path Event**: `tileLayer.once('tileload')` triggers dismissal immediately after the first center tile renders.



3. **1.2s Safety Timeout Guard**: Prevents infinite spinner locks on slow 2G/3G campus cellular connections; automatically reveals the interactive map canvas even if peripheral background tiles are still streaming.

### 196.2 Comprehensive Reverse-Engineering Methodology of MBSTU Wheels







To achieve true feature and data parity with the university's official transport system without unofficial breaking changes, the team reverse-engineered the production assets of `transport.mbstu.ac.bd/MBSTU-Wheels`.







#### A. Static Bundle Scraping & Next.js Decompilation



1. **Target Identification**:



   - The production portal uses Next.js with client-side route chunks under `/_next/static/chunks/`.



   - Automated scripts (`scripts/download_mbstu_chunks.py`, `scripts/analyze_chunks.py`) retrieved and parsed the webpack manifest and individual page chunks:



     - `pages/index-[hash].js`: Landing page, fleet overview, and static stoppage coordinates.



     - `pages/transit-[hash].js`: Map initialization, Leaflet tile layer definitions, vehicle state machines.



     - `pages/_app-[hash].js`: Socket.IO client setup and global notification contexts.







2. **Corridor Geometry & Coordinate Extraction**:



   - `scripts/extract_dir.py` and `scripts/chunk_strings.py` searched for coordinate arrays and extracted `polyline.json`, uncovering the ground-truth **80-vertex road-following polyline** running between Santosh Campus and Tangail Old Bus Stand.



   - Verified that earlier naive attempts using 6-12 straight-line segments caused the bus line to deflect into agricultural fields and bodies of water. The extracted 80 coordinates perfectly follow the asphalt curves of the Tangail-Santosh Highway.







3. **Stoppage Extraction & Alignment**:



   - Extracted 28 physical stoppage markers (`scripts/extract_vehicles.py`), validating Bengali labels, English aliases, and decimal coordinates:



     - Station 0: Santosh Campus (MBSTU Gate) `[24.2361, 89.8925]`



     - Station 7: Kagmari More `[24.2415, 89.9012]`



     - Station 14: Baby Stand `[24.2482, 89.9120]`



     - Station 21: Nirala More `[24.2503, 89.9142]`



     - Station 27: New Bus Terminal `[24.2610, 89.9285]`







#### B. Socket.IO Protocol Handshake & Wire Contract



1. **Endpoint Probing (`scripts/test_socketio.py`, `scripts/test_ws_payload.mjs`)**:



   - Probed `https://transport.mbstu.ac.bd/socket.io/` using Engine.IO v4 protocol:



     - Initial HTTP Long-Polling handshake: `GET /socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&t=...`



     - Upgraded to WebSocket: `GET /socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&sid=...`



   - Discovered that the server broadcasts real-time telemetry on the custom event: `live-bus-data`.







2. **Real-Time Telemetry Contract Schema**:



   ```typescript



   interface UpstreamBusPayload {



     id: string;               // Vehicle identifier (e.g. "MBSTU-BUS-01", "DHANSHIRI")



     name: string;             // Display name (e.g. "?????????", "??????", "???????")



     lat: number;              // High-precision WGS84 latitude



     lng: number;              // High-precision WGS84 longitude



     speed: number;            // Current speed in km/h



     heading: number;          // Course over ground (0 - 360 degrees)



     isActive: boolean;        // Operational toggle



     driverContact?: string;   // Optional phone number for emergencies



     currentStationIndex: number; // Index into 28-station array



     nextStationIndex: number;    // Approaching destination index



     updatedAt: string;        // UTC timestamp



   }



   ```
