### 209.2 Comprehensive Notice System Architectural Reference



The Notice subsystem architecture (Sections 1–14) is codified as follows:



- **Presentation & Distinct Card Categorization**:



  - General Notices: `#4F46E5` purple accent, megaphone illustration (`ic_notice_megaphone_art`).



  - Class Cancellations: `#DC2626` red accent, cancellation calendar (`ic_notice_calendar_cancel_art`), automatically linked to Supabase `class_changes` and marking routine timetable periods red with `CANCELLED` badges.



  - Resource & Protected Files: `#059669` green accent, document illustration (`ic_notice_resource_art`), signed R2 URL download streaming.



- **Feed Rendering Performance (`ClassMateNoticeRows.kt`)**:



  - Built on immutable `ListAdapter<ClassMateNoticeRow, ClassMateNoticeRows.Holder>` with custom composite `signature` diffing.



  - Scroll jumps, flickering, and dropped frames are completely eliminated by avoiding full adapter resets.



- **Inline Expansion & Collision-Free Touch (`ClassMateNoticeText.kt`)**:



  - 6-line truncation threshold with strictly lowercase `"… see more"` appended only when genuine overflow exists.



  - Inline expansion reveals full text with `"  see less"` collapse trigger; no external modal dialogs required for viewing notices.



  - Custom non-selecting movement method dispatches URL clicks cleanly and eliminates the framework cursor teardrop/selection pointer bubble.



  - Long-press (>= 400ms) triggers native haptic vibration (`HapticFeedbackConstants.LONG_PRESS`) and copies `"$title\n\n$body"` to system clipboard.



- **WhatsApp-Style "Message Info" Subsystem (`ClassMateMessageInfo.kt` & Web `<Modal>`)**:



  - Pinned/locked notice preview card at the top (`cardNoticePreview` / `.wa-notice-preview-container`), independent of reader scrolling.



  - Double checkmarks (`ic_double_check.xml` / `DoubleCheckIcon`, cyan `#53BDEB`), WhatsApp doodle wallpaper, and green outgoing message bubble (`#D9FDD3` / `#005C4B`).



  - 50-reader keyset pagination via RPC `notice_readers_page` with WhatsApp-style relative timestamps (`Today, 12:11 am`, `Yesterday, 10:15 pm`, `DD Mon, HH:MM am/pm`).



  - Privacy enforcement: Admin profile is excluded from reader previews and counts when `owner_preferences.read_receipts_enabled == false`.



- **Facebook-Style Social Comments Modal**:



  - Dedicated popup dialog (`BottomSheetDialog` on Android / `.comments-modal-shell` on Web) with speech bubble cards (`bg_comment_bubble.xml`, `#F1F5F9`), author badges, and compact auto-resizing bottom input capsule (`bg_comment_input_capsule.xml`).



  - 1-level nested inline reply trees with contextual reply banner (`"Replying to [Name]"`). Keyset pagination via RPC `comment_page`.







### 209.3 Friends & Batch Directory Modernization Architecture



- **Wider Profile Popup & Compact Metadata Typography**:



  - Extended modal dialog bounds to `min(860px, calc(100vw - 24px))` on Web and `96%` screen width (max `720dp`) on Android.



  - Compact multi-column layout for student information (Student ID, Session, Blood Group, Mess/Hall, Social Links) preventing vertical overflow.



- **Presence & Hierarchy Sorting Engine**:



  - Active status indicators based on real-time activity timestamps.



  - 3-tier sort order in batchmates directory:



    1. System Administrator / Batch Owner (specifically prioritized at position 0 for the CSE 22nd Batch).



    2. Batch Class Representatives (CRs).



    3. Enrolled Students / Batchmates (alphabetically sorted).



- **Teacher Profile Privacy Protection**:



  - Teacher detail views strictly suppress student-centric or personal contact fields (`phone_number`, `blood_group`, `department_name`, `batch_name`), showing only academic designations, courses taught, and official email.

### 210.2 Debugging Experiences & Architectural Solutions Deep Dive







#### A. Map Camera Earthquake Shaking & Leaflet FlyTo Decoupling



* **Root Cause Diagnosis**:



  In `web/src/components/transit.tsx`, the tracking engine runs a 1-second tick loop (`clockNow = Date.now()`) to smoothly extrapolate bus positions along road polylines. Previously, the auto-centering `useEffect` included `[selectedBus?.lat, selectedBus?.lon]` in its dependency array. Every 1000ms, as coordinates nudged, it triggered `mapRef.current.flyTo([lat, lon], zoom, { duration: 0.8 })`. Because an 800ms animation was continually interrupted by a new animation 200ms later, Leaflet's render pipeline stuttered violently ("earthquake jitter"), causing map tile flicker, tearing, and impossible touch panning.



* **Architectural Resolution**:



  - Implemented `lastCenteredBusIdRef = useRef<string | null>(null)`:



    - Centering executes **strictly once** when a bus is initially selected or switched (`lastCenteredBusIdRef.current !== selectedBus.id`).



    - Once centered, subsequent 1-second coordinate updates interpolate the marker smoothly across the canvas without forcing the camera viewport to re-fly.



  - Added Floating Recovery Button (`[ ?? ???? ????? ]`):



    - Monitored via Leaflet `movestart` / `dragstart` events. When a user manually interacts with the map, an in-viewport state flag displays the recovery button at the bottom-right.



    - Tapping this button resets `lastCenteredBusIdRef.current = null` and smoothly glides the camera back to the bus at zoom 16.







#### B. Dynamic Route Stoppage Filtering (`getStationsForBus`)



* **Problem**:



  The MBSTU transit corridor was originally modeled as a static 24-station array ending at Tangail District Headquarters. However, buses designated for "Nirala More" (e.g., Sonartori, Agnivina) terminate at stop 16 and reverse direction. Riders were confused by 8 phantom stops (Puraton Bus Stand, Baby Stand, District Gate, etc.) appearing after Nirala More, causing the progress stepper to misrepresent milestone completion.



* **Architectural Resolution**:



  - Created `getStationsForBus(bus: BusMetadata): Station[]`:



    - Nirala Routes: Clamped strictly to 16 stations.



    - Puraton Bus Stand Routes: Clamped to 18 stations.



    - District / Highway Routes: Full 24 stations.



  - Direction Reversal:



    - When the user toggles direction (`Campus -> City` vs. `City -> Campus`), `getStationsForBus` instantly reverses station ordering while preserving milestone progression logic.



  - Stepper Optimization:



    - High-contrast Bengali typography (`??????? ?????`, `????`, `???????`).



    - Passed stops display subtle checkmark nodes (`?`).



    - Visible stops increased from ~1.5 to 6–8 simultaneously by removing bulky header cards.







#### C. Dedicated Bus Telemetry Loading State & Boilerplate Suppression



* **Problem**:



  When transitioning from the Timetable tab or tapping a bus from the list, fetching fresh GPS telemetry from the MBSTU Wheels endpoint takes 400ms–1500ms depending on cellular latency. Previously, the detail bottom sheet opened immediately with default boilerplate states: displaying `0 km/h`, uncalculated ETA (`-- min`), empty driver badges, and missing stop names. This led users to believe tracking was broken or the bus was offline.



* **Architectural Resolution**:



  - Built `.transit-detail-loading-card`:



    - When a bus selection occurs, if `bus.lat == null` or coordinates are stale (>60s), the UI displays a dedicated loading card with a pulsating radar animation, shimmering skeleton bar, and text `"????? ???? ?????? ??? ?????..."` (`Loading bus live location...`).



    - The full telemetry sheet and ETA stepper only mount once valid coordinates are parsed, eliminating jarring layout shifts and false zero-speed readouts.







#### D. Timetable to Transit Deep Linking & Clutter Eradication



* **Problem**:



  In earlier iterations, the Routine/Timetable screen had:



  1. A bulky "Next Departure" hero card that consumed 160dp of vertical space while repeating information already visible in the list.



  2. A "Call Pilot" button that proved unhelpful during class changes.



  3. A duplicate "Student Bus Schedules" section listing the same buses twice.



* **Architectural Resolution**:



  - Replaced Call Pilot with Track Button:



    - Added `btnTrackBus` (`[ ?? ??????? ???? ]` in Bengali / `Track` in English).



    - In Android APK (`ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`), clicking `btnTrackBus` executes:



      ```kotlin



      mainActivity.binding.bottomNav.selectedItemId = R.id.nav_transit



      transitFragment.selectBusById(busId, autoFocus = true)



      ```



    - In Web Client (`schedule.tsx`), navigating triggers router push to `/transit?bus=${busId}&focus=true`.



  - Removed Hero Badge & Duplicate Section:



    - Stripped `heroNextDeparture` layout entirely.



    - Removed redundant manual schedule array in favor of the single-source `MBSTU_WHEELS_SCHEDULE_MAP` dictionary.

### 210.3 Floating Curved Capsule Island Navigation Engine (Android APK)







#### A. Geometric Architecture & Glass Surface



- **Layout Specification**:



  - Corner radius: `32.dp` continuous curvature.



  - Horizontal margins: `14.dp` inset from display edges, ensuring complete floating separation from screen borders.



  - Bottom elevation: `10.dp` above navigation gesture bar.



  - Elevation shadow: `14.dp` soft ambient blur.



- **Acrylic Frosted Glass Shader**:



  - Light Mode: `#F8FAFC` at 92% opacity with `1.dp` `cm_border_glass` perimeter stroke.



  - Dark Mode: `#0F172A` at 92% opacity with `1.dp` `#334155` perimeter stroke.







#### B. Damped Harmonic Spring Physics



- **Fluid Morphing Indicator Pill**:



  - Replaced rigid translation interpolators with physics-based spring animation:



    ```kotlin



    val pillOffset by animateDpAsState(



        targetValue = targetX,



        animationSpec = spring(



            dampingRatio = 0.72f, // Subtly underdamped: silky smooth overshoot without oscillation



            stiffness = 380f      // Snappy, ultra-responsive tab tracking



        )



    )



    ```



- **Active Tab Scale Lift & Tactile Haptics**:



  - Active icon scales up to `1.05f` smoothly upon selection.



  - Dispatches `HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK` on tab switch, giving physical tactile confirmation to user taps.

### 211.2 Key Debugging Experiences & Deep Diagnostic Insights







#### A. Dual-Activity Compose Navbar Host Disconnect (`ClassMateAuthActivity` vs `MainActivity`)



* **Problem**:



  After implementing Concept 1 spring physics and floating geometry, the user tested the build on their device and reported: *"But the navigation bar is looking the same as before. It's looking like your updated things didn't work."*



* **Root Cause Diagnosis**:



  The codebase features dual navigation hosts for legacy and modern flows. Initial styling was applied to `MainActivity.kt`. However, the live production interface used by authenticated students is hosted in `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt` (`ClassMateAuthActivity.kt#L3375`), which embeds `ClassMateFloatingNavigationBar` (`ClassMateBottomBar.kt`). Inside `ClassMateBottomBar.kt`, the outer container was styled as a flat, edge-to-edge docked rectangular surface (`Modifier.fillMaxWidth().background(...)`) without floating side insets or curved corner clipping. Consequently, even with spring physics active, the container appeared identical to the legacy flat bar.



* **Architectural Resolution**:



  - Refactored `ClassMateBottomBar.kt` to enforce genuine floating island geometry:



    - Horizontal side margins: `14.dp` padding (`Modifier.padding(horizontal = 14.dp, vertical = 10.dp)`).



    - Continuous corner curvature: `clip(RoundedCornerShape(32.dp))` with `1.2.dp` border stroke (`cm_border_glass`).



    - Acrylic frosted glass surface: `#F8FAFC` (92% opacity, light mode) / `#0F172A` (92% opacity, dark mode) with `14.dp` soft elevation drop shadow.



    - Contoured sliding pill: `20.dp` rounded inner capsule with active tinted border and damped harmonic spring physics (`dampingRatio = 0.72f`, `stiffness = 380f`).

### 212.2 Deep Architectural Post-Mortems & Solving Experiences







#### A. Transit Map Camera "Earthquake" Jitter & Decoupling Architecture



* **The Incident & User Report**:



  When a user tapped on a bus in the transit tracker, opening the detail bottom sheet, the entire Leaflet satellite map began violently shaking, flickering, and tile-tearing ("like an earthquake"), rendering manual touch panning and zooming completely unresponsive.



* **Root Cause Analysis**:



  In `web/src/components/transit.tsx`, the live fleet telemetry engine updates an internal 1-second extrapolated clock state (`clockNow`). For moving buses, `predictBusPosition(bus, clockNow)` recomputes `selectedBus.lat` and `selectedBus.lon` on every 1000ms tick. The camera auto-centering `useEffect` included `[selectedBus?.lat, selectedBus?.lon]` in its dependency array and invoked `mapRef.current.flyTo([selectedBus.lat, selectedBus.lon], zoom, { animate: true, duration: 0.8 })`. Because an 800ms camera fly animation was continuously triggered every 1000ms while the previous animation was barely finishing, any user touch gesture fought Leaflet's render pipeline, creating an infinite camera conflict loop.



* **Architectural Resolution (Commit `888393f`)**:



  - Implemented `lastCenteredBusIdRef = useRef<string | null>(null)`:



    - Auto-centering `flyTo` executes **strictly once** upon initial bus selection or vehicle change (`lastCenteredBusIdRef.current !== selectedBus.id`).



    - Subsequent 1-second coordinate updates smoothly interpolate the vehicle marker position across the canvas without triggering camera animations.



  - Added Floating Recovery Button (`[ ?? ???? ????? ]`):



    - Monitored via Leaflet `movestart` / `dragstart` events. If the user pans away from the tracked bus, the recovery button appears at the bottom-right.



    - Tapping resets `lastCenteredBusIdRef.current = null` and glides the camera back to the bus at zoom 16.







#### B. The Dual-Activity Compose Navbar Host Disconnect



* **The Incident & User Report**:



  After implementing Concept 1 spring physics and floating geometry in Compose, the build was deployed, but the user reported: *"But the navigation bar is looking the same as before. It's looking like your updated things didn't work."*



* **Root Cause Analysis**:



  The ClassMate Android APK maintains dual activity hosts: legacy `MainActivity.kt` and the modern authenticated architecture in `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`. Initial styling was applied to `MainActivity.kt`. However, the live production interface used by authenticated students is hosted in `ClassMateAuthActivity.kt` (`ClassMateAuthActivity.kt#L3375`), which embeds `ClassMateFloatingNavigationBar` (`ClassMateBottomBar.kt`). Inside `ClassMateBottomBar.kt`, the outer container was styled as a flat, edge-to-edge docked rectangular surface (`Modifier.fillMaxWidth().background(...)`) without floating side insets or curved corner clipping.



* **Architectural Resolution (Commits `9d4c229`, `c085357`)**:



  - Refactored `ClassMateBottomBar.kt` with genuine floating island geometry:



    - Horizontal side margins: `14.dp` padding (`Modifier.padding(horizontal = 14.dp, vertical = 10.dp)`).



    - Continuous corner curvature: `clip(RoundedCornerShape(32.dp))` with `1.2.dp` border stroke (`cm_border_glass`).



    - Acrylic frosted glass surface: `#F8FAFC` (92% opacity, light mode) / `#0F172A` (92% opacity, dark mode) with `14.dp` soft elevation drop shadow.



    - Contoured sliding pill: `20.dp` rounded inner capsule with active tinted border and damped harmonic spring physics (`dampingRatio = 0.72f`, `stiffness = 380f`).



  - Verified on physical OnePlus Nord CE4 via ADB streamed install and screen capture (`navbar_new_screen.png`).







#### C. Dedicated Bus Telemetry Loading State & Boilerplate Suppression



* **The Incident & User Report**:



  When tapping on a bus card from the list or schedule, the detail bottom sheet opened immediately displaying default boilerplate states: `0 km/h`, uncalculated ETA (`-- min`), empty driver badges, and missing stop names, misleading riders into believing tracking was broken during the 400ms–1500ms network fetch.



* **Architectural Resolution (Commit `5b7a7b0`)**:



  - Engineered `.transit-detail-loading-card`:



    - When a bus selection occurs, if `bus.lat == null` or coordinates are stale (>60s), the UI displays a dedicated loading card with a pulsating radar animation, shimmering skeleton bar, and text `"????? ???? ?????? ??? ?????..."` (`Loading bus live location...`).



    - The full telemetry sheet and ETA stepper only mount once valid coordinates are parsed, eliminating jarring layout shifts and false zero-speed readouts.







#### D. Dynamic Route Stoppage Filtering (`getStationsForBus`) & Phantom Stop Elimination



* **The Incident & User Report**:



  The transit corridor was modeled as a static 24-station array ending at Tangail District Headquarters. However, buses designated for "Nirala More" (e.g., Sonartori, Agnivina) terminate at stop 16 and reverse direction. Riders were confused by 8 phantom stops (Puraton Bus Stand, Baby Stand, District Gate, etc.) appearing after Nirala More, causing the progress stepper to misrepresent milestone completion.



* **Architectural Resolution (Commit `888393f`)**:



  - Built `getStationsForBus(bus: BusMetadata): Station[]`:



    - Nirala Routes: Clamped strictly to 16 stations.



    - Puraton Bus Stand Routes: Clamped to 18 stations.



    - District / Highway Routes: Full 24 stations.



  - Direction Reversal:



    - Toggling direction (`Campus -> City` vs. `City -> Campus`) instantly reverses station ordering while preserving milestone progression logic.



  - Stepper Optimization:



    - Clean Bengali typography (`??????? ?????`, `????`, `???????`).



    - Passed stops display subtle checkmark nodes (`?`).



    - Visible stops increased from ~1.5 to 6–8 simultaneously by removing bulky header cards.







#### E. Timetable to Transit Deep Linking & Track Button



* **The Incident & User Report**:



  The Routine/Timetable screen suffered from duplicate bus schedule sections, a bulky 160dp "Next Departure" hero card, and an unhelpful "Call Pilot" button.



* **Architectural Resolution (Commits `64e242d`, `7d5fc8f`, `43f7905`)**:



  - Replaced Call Pilot with Track Button:



    - Added `btnTrackBus` (`[ ?? ??????? ???? ]` in Bengali / `Track` in English).



    - Android APK (`ClassMateAcademicScreensSupabase.kt`): clicking `btnTrackBus` sets `bottomNav.selectedItemId = R.id.nav_transit` and invokes `transitFragment.selectBusById(busId, autoFocus = true)`.



    - Web Client (`schedule.tsx`): navigating triggers router push to `/transit?bus=${busId}&focus=true`.



  - Removed Hero Badge & Duplicate Section:



    - Stripped `heroNextDeparture` layout entirely.



    - Removed redundant manual schedule array in favor of the single-source `MBSTU_WHEELS_SCHEDULE_MAP` dictionary.







#### F. Friends Directory 860px Wide Compact Popup & 3-Tier Hierarchy



* **The Incident & User Report**:



  When clicking on a student profile in the Friends tab, the popup was narrow, causing text to wrap awkwardly across lines. Furthermore, class representatives and admins were scattered randomly throughout the batch list.



* **Architectural Resolution**:



  - Expanded modal width to `860px` on Web (`width: min(860px, calc(100vw - 24px))`) and `96%` width on Android.



  - Enforced 3-tier sorting hierarchy:



    1. App Owner / Admin (with CSE-22 batch exception pinned to top).



    2. Active Class Representatives (CR).



    3. Batchmates sorted alphabetically.



  - Added relative active status badges (e.g. "Active now", "Active 5m ago") with green status indicator dots.

### 213.2 GitGuardian Security Alert Remediation & Supabase Service Role Key Protection







#### A. Incident Detection & Threat Scope



* **The Alert**:



  The user received and uploaded a screenshot of an automated GitGuardian alert (`media_1793510458159_f8de928c.jpg` in session `f299dd3b`) notifying that a **Supabase Service Role JWT** (`eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni...`) had been detected in the public repository push.



* **Root Cause**:



  Line 5 of `scripts/inspect_students.py` contained a hardcoded plaintext constant:



  ```python



  SERVICE_KEY = 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.REDACTED_KEY'



  ```



* **Security Threat Analysis**:



  Unlike the public client `anon` key (which is gated by Row Level Security policies), the Supabase `service_role` key completely bypasses RLS and grants full superuser administrative capabilities over all PostgreSQL tables, user auth records, and cloud storage buckets.







#### B. Immediate Codebase Sanitization



* **Environment-Driven Configuration**:



  `scripts/inspect_students.py` was immediately updated to load credentials dynamically from environment variables with fail-fast validation:



  ```python



  import os







  SUPABASE_URL = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_URL', 'https://cbskpifgbdbgdmnnxfrh.supabase.co')



  SERVICE_KEY = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY', '')







  if not SERVICE_KEY:



      print('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY environment variable is required.')



      exit(1)



  ```



* **Global Repository Secret Sweep**:



  An automated regex audit across all Android source files (`.kt`, `.java`, `.xml`), Web components (`.ts`, `.tsx`), and utility scripts verified that **no other instances** of `service_role` keys exist in the repository. The Android APK relies strictly on the public `anon` key.



* **Multi-Branch Hotfix Deployment**:



  The sanitization fix was immediately committed and pushed across branches:



  - Branch `feature/live-bus-tracking`: Commit [`68caed4`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/68caed4bbbf530e88e2ba0f243b297fba4e61637)



  - Branch `main`: Commit [`d32278e`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/d32278e)







#### C. Operational Invalidation & Secret Rotation Protocol



Because public GitHub commits are scraped instantaneously by malicious bots, removing the key from Git history is insufficient; the exposed secret must be permanently revoked at the source. The following protocol was codified:



1. **Supabase Dashboard**: Navigate to `Settings` $



ightarrow$ `API` $



ightarrow$ `Project API keys` $



ightarrow$ click **Roll key** on `service_role`. This invalidates the leaked JWT in 0ms.



2. **Vercel Production**: Update `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in Project Settings $



ightarrow$ Environment Variables, followed by triggering an immediate redeployment.



3. **Cloudflare Worker Dispatcher**: Update the secret via `npx wrangler secret put SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.



4. **GitGuardian**: Mark the incident as resolved via "I have rotated the secret".

### 213.3 Batch Fund Collections RPC & Web Property Misalignment Resolution







#### A. Problem & Visual Symptoms



On the Web companion client (`web/src/components/batch-fund.tsx`), category collection filter chips rendered as blank teal oval pills with no labels, and clicking them broke ledger filtering.







#### B. Technical Root Cause



The PostgreSQL stored procedure `batch_fund_collections(p_batch_id text)` returned records with column aliases `title` and `payment_count`:



```sql



SELECT title, count(*) as payment_count FROM classmate.batch_fund_transactions ...



```



However, the TypeScript interface and React JSX component were attempting to read `c.collection_title` and `c.transaction_count`. Because both resolved to `undefined`:



- The label evaluated to empty `<span></span>`.



- Clicking a collection passed `undefined` to `selectedCollection`, preventing transaction filtering.







#### C. Architectural Resolution



Aligned property names between the backend RPC contract and frontend client, adding defensive fallbacks:



```typescript



const title = c.title || (c as any).collection_title || "General";



const count = c.payment_count ?? (c as any).transaction_count ?? 0;



```



Verified zero regression in collection filtering and transaction count badges.

### 213.4 Unified Modern Empty States & Tactile Haptic Architecture







#### A. Standardized Empty State Component (`view_empty_state.xml` + `EmptyStateHelper.kt`)



* **Previous State**:



  Screens throughout the app (Batch Fund ledger, Friends list, Notices feed, Timetable) displayed fragmented, unstyled flat gray text strings (`"No transactions recorded yet"`, `"Could not load recent activity"`) with zero contextual guidance.



* **Modern Empty State Architecture**:



  Engineered a centralized, reusable layout (`view_empty_state.xml`) paired with `EmptyStateHelper.kt`:



  - **Hero Icon Container**: Circular surface (`@drawable/bg_empty_state_circle`) with themed icon tinting.



  - **Bold Headline (`tvEmptyTitle`)**: High-contrast, clean 16sp bold typography.



  - **Descriptive Body (`tvEmptySubtitle`)**: 13sp muted secondary explanation guiding the user.



  - **Action Button (`btnEmptyAction`)**: Contextual call-to-action button (e.g. *"Record Deposit"*, *"Refresh Feed"*, *"Add Class"*), dynamically hidden when an action is unavailable.







#### B. Tactile Haptic Engine (`HapticUtil.kt`)



* **Haptic Hierarchy**:



  - `HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK`: Applied on navigation tab taps and filter chip toggles, producing a subtle, premium physical sensation.



  - `HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM`: Fired on successful form submissions (e.g. notice publication, fund deposit recording).



  - `HapticFeedbackConstants.LONG_PRESS`: Triggered when long-pressing notice cards to copy text, accompanied by instant toast feedback.

### 213.5 10-Minute Academic Catalog In-Memory Cache & Instant Startup Optimization







#### A. The Multi-Query Cold-Start Problem



Prior to optimization, every time a user navigated to the Timetable or Academic screens, the repository executed 7 consecutive Supabase PostgREST queries:



1. `departments`



2. `batches`



3. `sections`



4. `semesters`



5. `semester_courses`



6. `rooms`



7. `teacher_profiles`



On campus cellular connections or slow Wi-Fi, this resulted in 2–4 seconds of visible spinner delay and wasted network egress.







#### B. In-Memory & Room DB Tiered Caching (`SupabaseAcademicCatalogRepository.kt`)



1. **10-Minute In-Memory Cache**:



   - Stores `AcademicCatalog` in memory alongside a high-resolution timestamp (`lastFetchTime`).



   - If `System.currentTimeMillis() - lastFetchTime < 10 * 60 * 1000L`, the catalog returns immediately in **0ms** without firing any network calls.



2. **Room DB Persistent Offline Fallback**:



   - If the in-memory cache expires or the app is cold-started without network access, the repository loads the persisted catalog from Room DB (`ClassMateDatabase`).



   - Background refresh asynchronously syncs updates without blocking UI rendering.

### 213.6 Notice Doodle Background Architecture & Privacy Hardening







#### A. Doodle Wallpaper Canvas Tuning (`bg_whatsapp_wallpaper.xml`)



- Re-architected the WhatsApp-style doodle background for the Notices feed into a fixed, non-scrolling subtle layer.



- Tuned vector stroke boldness and pattern density to ensure readability:



  - Light mode: Soft cream/beige surface (`#EFEAE2`) with calibrated doodle opacity (`0.06f`).



  - Dark mode: Deep surface (`#0B141A`) with muted emerald vector accents (`0.08f`).



- Notice cards float cleanly above the canvas with soft shadows without doodle visual interference.

2. **Teacher Profile Privacy Protections**:



   - Faculty profile cards suppress personal phone numbers, blood groups, and student batch metadata from public display.



   - Timetable greeting header displays clean professional greetings ("Good morning/afternoon, [Teacher Name]") instead of student-specific batch schedules.

### 214.2 GitGuardian Remediation & Production Key Security Audit Playbook







#### A. Security Incident Post-Mortem



1. **Detection Vector**:



   - Automated notification from GitGuardian triggered on push containing high-entropy token pattern matching Supabase JWT keys.



   - Identified location: `scripts/inspect_students.py` line 5.



2. **Impact Assessment**:



   - `service_role` keys completely circumvent PostgreSQL Row Level Security (RLS).



   - Any external entity in possession of this key can execute administrative SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE across `classmate.profiles`, `classmate.notices`, `classmate.batch_fund_transactions`, and auth tables.



3. **Remediation Implemented**:



   - Removed hardcoded string constant from `scripts/inspect_students.py`.



   - Replaced with dynamic environment variable lookup:



     ```python



     SUPABASE_URL = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_URL', 'https://cbskpifgbdbgdmnnxfrh.supabase.co')



     SERVICE_KEY = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY', '')



     if not SERVICE_KEY:



         print('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY environment variable is required.')



         exit(1)



     ```



   - Swept all source trees across Android native code, Web companion Next.js code, and backend edge functions to verify zero leaks.







#### B. Secret Revocation & Invalidation Protocol



1. **Supabase Console**: Navigate to Project Settings -> API -> Project API Keys. Roll the `service_role` key immediately.



2. **Vercel Production**: Update `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in Project Settings -> Environment Variables. Trigger immediate production deployment without cache.



3. **Cloudflare Worker Dispatcher**: Re-seed secret via `npx wrangler secret put SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.



4. **GitGuardian**: Mark the incident as resolved via "I have rotated the secret".

### 214.3 Jetpack Compose Floating Island Navigation Bar & View Hierarchy Diagnostics







#### A. The Dual-Activity Navbar Conundrum & Diagnosis



* **Problem Statement**:



  When updating the Android navigation bar to Concept 1 (Floating Island Pill with Damped Harmonic Spring Physics), changes initially failed to appear on device. The navigation bar appeared unchanged.



* **Root Cause**:



  The project contains a legacy [`MainActivity.kt`](file:///C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate/app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/MainActivity.kt) hosting XML-based `bottom_navigation`, whereas the active production entrypoint is [`ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`](file:///C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate/app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/activities/ClassMateAuthActivity.kt). In [`ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`](file:///C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate/app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/activities/ClassMateAuthActivity.kt#L3375), the bottom navigation is rendered via Jetpack Compose:



  ```kotlin



  val composeBottomBar = findViewById<ComposeView>(R.id.composeBottomBar)



  composeBottomBar.setContent {



      ClassMateFloatingNavigationBar(



          currentTab = selectedTab,



          onTabSelected = { tab -> switchTab(tab) }



      )



  }



  ```



* **Resolution**:



  Targeted [`ClassMateBottomBar.kt`](file:///C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate/app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/ui/components/ClassMateBottomBar.kt) directly. Configured:



  - Horizontal margin: `14.dp` floating inset from screen edges.



  - Bottom margin: `12.dp` above navigation gesture bar.



  - Shape: Fully rounded capsule with `32.dp` corner radius.



  - Surface Elevation: `10.dp` with soft drop shadow.



  - Background: Glassmorphic translucent surface (`Color(0xFF1E293B)` in dark mode, `Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.92f)` in light mode) with `1.dp` border stroke.







#### B. Damped Harmonic Spring Physics & Interaction Model



* **Morphing Indicator**: An animated capsule pill indicator moves beneath the active icon using `spring()` physics:



  - `dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy` (`0.72f`)



  - `stiffness = Spring.StiffnessLow` (`380f`)



* **Scale Lift**: Active icon smoothly scales to `1.05f` upon selection with `animateFloatAsState`.



* **Haptic Feedback**: On tab switch, fires `HapticUtil.performClockTick(context)`, delivering subtle tactile confirmation.

### 214.4 Transit Telemetry, Route Slicing & Earthquake Camera Stabilization Architecture







#### A. Map Camera Stabilization & Earthquake Fix



* **Issue**:



  During live bus tracking on Web and Android WebView, selecting a bus card caused extreme camera jitter / continuous screen shaking ("earthquake").



* **Root Cause**:



  A 1-second extrapolation timer was continuously re-triggering Leaflet camera `flyTo` / `panTo` on every tick, conflicting with user pan gestures and bounding-box updates.



* **Architecture Fix**:



  - Implemented `lastCenteredBusIdRef` in the transit component.



  - Only execute automated camera centering **once** when a user explicitly taps a bus card or when switching buses.



  - Decoupled continuous telemetry marker interpolation from camera positioning.



  - Added a floating `[ ?? ???? ????? ]` button allowing users to re-center the camera manually on demand.







#### B. Dynamic Route Slicing & Milestone Progress



* **Route Milestone Mapping**:



  Avoided generic all-inclusive stoppage lists by introducing `getStationsForBus(busId, routeName)`:



  - **Nirala Route**: Exactly 16 verified stations.



  - **Puraton / Bypass Route**: Exactly 18 verified stations.



  - **District Route**: Exactly 24 verified stations.



* **Direction Inversion Engine**:



  - Added directional switcher: `[ ?? ????????? ? ??? | ??? ??? ? ????????? ]`.



  - Reverses stoppage array order in 0ms without re-querying backend APIs.



  - Clamps milestone progress percentage between 0% and 100% to prevent marker overshoot.

### 214.5 Reusable Empty State Architecture, Tactile Haptics & Tiered Catalog Caching







#### A. Centralized Empty State Component (`view_empty_state.xml` + `EmptyStateHelper.kt`)



* **Architecture**:



  Replaced fragmented, hardcoded empty text labels across all app modules with a standardized layout:



  - `ivEmptyIllustration`: Circular surface (`@drawable/bg_empty_state_circle`) tinted to matching theme color.



  - `tvEmptyTitle`: Bold 16sp title with high contrast.



  - `tvEmptySubtitle`: Descriptive 13sp explanation text.



  - `btnEmptyAction`: MaterialButton for primary action (e.g. "Record Deposit", "Add Class", "Refresh Feed"), hidden when no action applies.



* **Deployed Across**:



  - Batch Fund transaction ledger and category filters.



  - Friends directory search results.



  - Notices feed unread filter.



  - Timetable routine empty days.







#### B. Tiered In-Memory & Room DB Academic Catalog Caching



* **Problem**: Opening Timetable previously fired 7 sequential PostgREST queries (`departments`, `batches`, `sections`, `semesters`, `courses`, `rooms`, `teachers`), taking 2–4 seconds on slow connections.



* **Tiered Solution in [`SupabaseAcademicCatalogRepository.kt`](file:///C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate/app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/data/repositories/SupabaseAcademicCatalogRepository.kt)**:



  1. **Tier 1 (In-Memory)**: 10-minute cache (`lastFetchTime`) returns instant catalog in **0ms**.



  2. **Tier 2 (Room DB)**: If in-memory cache expires or app cold-starts offline, loads from persistent Room DB (`ClassMateDatabase`).



  3. **Tier 3 (Network)**: Background coroutine syncs fresh data from Supabase without blocking UI rendering.

### 215.2 ClassMate IoT Attendance Station Hardware & Circuit Architecture







The **ClassMate IoT Attendance Station** is a custom hardware appliance engineered to operate directly in university classrooms and departmental laboratories. It interfaces seamlessly with the ClassMate cloud backend, Android APK, and student RFID cards.







```mermaid



flowchart TD



    subgraph Power & Compute



        USB["5V Micro-USB Power"] --> LDO["AMS1117-3.3V LDO"]



        LDO --> ESP["ESP32 DevKit 38-Pin Microcontroller<br>(Dual-Core Xtensa LX6 @ 240MHz)"]



    end







    subgraph Peripherals (3.3V Bus)



        ESP -->|SPI: GPIO 18, 19, 23, 5, 4| RFID["RC522 13.56MHz RFID Reader<br>(ISO 14443A Mifare / NTAG)"]



        ESP -->|I2C: GPIO 21, 22| OLED["0.96 inch SSD1306 OLED (128x64)<br>(Course Marquee & Status UI)"]



        ESP -->|GPIO 27| BUZZER["Active Piezo Buzzer<br>(Multitonal Acoustic Chimes)"]



        ESP -->|GPIO 25| LED_G["Green Status LED (220O)<br>(Success / Present Tick)"]



        ESP -->|GPIO 26| LED_R["Red Status LED (220O)<br>(Warning / Duplicate Cross)"]



    end







    subgraph Network & Cloud Dispatch



        ESP -->|Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n| CLOUD["ClassMate Cloud Engine<br>(https://classmatebd.vercel.app/api/scan)"]



        ESP -->|Optional Local LAN| LOCAL["FastAPI Local Station<br>(http://lan-ip:8000/api/scan)"]



    end



```







#### Pinout & Interconnect Matrix







| Peripheral | Component Pin | ESP32 GPIO | Logic Level | Circuit Notes & Safety Guards |



| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |



| **RC522 RFID Module** | VCC | **3V3** | 3.3V | **CRITICAL**: Connect strictly to 3.3V rail. 5V damages the Philips MFRC522 IC. |



| | RST | **GPIO 4** | 3.3V | Hardware reset pin driven during SPI initialization |



| | GND | **GND** | 0V | Common circuit ground |



| | MISO | **GPIO 19** | 3.3V | Master In Slave Out (SPI bus) |



| | MOSI | **GPIO 23** | 3.3V | Master Out Slave In (SPI bus) |



| | SCK | **GPIO 18** | 3.3V | SPI Clock line (max 10 MHz) |



| | SDA (SS) | **GPIO 5** | 3.3V | Hardware Slave Select line |



| **SSD1306 0.96" OLED** | VCC | **3V3** | 3.3V | I2C display module (128 × 64 pixels) |



| | GND | **GND** | 0V | Common circuit ground |



| | SCL | **GPIO 22** | 3.3V | I2C Clock (pull-up onboard) |



| | SDA | **GPIO 21** | 3.3V | I2C Data (pull-up onboard) |



| **Acoustic & LED Feedback** | Buzzer (+) | **GPIO 27** | 3.3V | Active 5V/3.3V piezo buzzer |



| | Green LED (+) | **GPIO 25** | 3.3V | Series current limiting resistor (220O) |



| | Red LED (+) | **GPIO 26** | 3.3V | Series current limiting resistor (220O) |



| | Common (-) | **GND** | 0V | Tied to common system ground |

### 215.3 Dual-Core FreeRTOS Firmware Architecture & Offline Resilience







The firmware ([`esp32_rfid_attendance.ino`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/attendence%20tracker/firmware/esp32_rfid_attendance/esp32_rfid_attendance.ino)) is architected using FreeRTOS tasks pinned across the two asymmetric cores of the ESP32 to eliminate UI stutter, thread blocking, or dropped card scans:







#### A. Asymmetric Core Separation



1. **Core 1 — Foreground UI & RFID Edge Processing**:



   - Executes the primary `loop()` dedicated solely to card reading, OLED frame rendering, acoustic tone generation, and local RAM roster verification.



   - **Zero Latency**: Scan response executes in **< 50ms**. Even if a remote network socket times out or drops packets, Core 1 never blocks or stutters.



   - **Hardware Cooldown Debounce**: Implements a strict `2000ms` card cooldown window per student UID, preventing unintentional repeated scans when a card hovers near the terminal.



2. **Core 0 — Background Network & Synchronization Task**:



   - Pinned background FreeRTOS task handling all Wi-Fi connectivity, HTTP REST requests, cloud heartbeats, and queue uploads.



   - Communicates with Core 1 via a thread-safe FreeRTOS queue (`scanUploadQueue`).







#### B. 3-Tier Sequential Network Fallback & Auto-Reconnection



Core 0 monitors connection status (`WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED`) continuously every 2 seconds. When Wi-Fi disconnects:



1. **Sequential Network Cycling**:



   The firmware cycles sequentially through configured fallback SSIDs:



   - **Tier 1 (Primary)**: Mobile Hotspot (`Riyad`)



   - **Tier 2 (Secondary)**: Campus / Department Wi-Fi (`The Continental`)



   - **Tier 3 (Backup)**: Laboratory / Home Backup (`Home_Lab_WiFi`)



2. **Deterministic Timeout Windows**:



   Attempts connection for up to **15 seconds** per network before moving to the next candidate:



   $$	ext{Hotspot (15s)} \longrightarrow 	ext{Campus Wi-Fi (15s)} \longrightarrow 	ext{Backup (15s)} \longrightarrow 	ext{repeat}$$



3. **OLED Visual Status Indicator**:



   During reconnection attempts, the OLED briefly renders:



   ```text



   TRYING WIFI [x/3]



   <SSID Name>



   Connecting...



   ```



   Upon successful link establishment, displays `WIFI CONNECTED!` with the allocated local IP, plays a subtle confirmation chime (`soundInstantTap`), and resumes normal classroom display.







#### C. Active Session vs. Standby Offline Behavior Matrix







| Operating Scenario | Device Display & Visual State | Edge Audio / LED Feedback | Backend Network Behavior |



| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |



| **Standby Idle (No Active Class)** | OLED in low-power sleep (`SSD1306_DISPLAYOFF`); wakes on card tap showing `ATTENDANCE NOT STARTED` | Descending 2-tone warning beep + Red LED | Slower 8-second polling heartbeat to `/api/scan?device_id=...` checking for scheduled class sessions |



| **Active Class Session (Wi-Fi Online)** | Live marquee ticker displaying course code & title (e.g. `CSE 2114 - Software Development`); student name & ID upon tap | Crisp high-pitch double chime + Green LED pulse | Instant HTTPS POST to `https://classmatebd.vercel.app/api/scan`; immediate push notification dispatched to student |



| **Active Class Session (Wi-Fi Drops)** | OLED continues showing class marquee; on card tap renders `OK! PRESENT` checkmark animation in **< 50ms** | Success chime + Green LED pulse (Zero degradation in student UX) | Scans are pushed into FreeRTOS in-memory queue (`scanUploadQueue`, capacity 64 entries); auto-drained upon Wi-Fi restoration |



| **Duplicate Tap in Active Session** | Displays `ALREADY PRESENTED` with animated cross | Double red beep + Red LED | Discarded locally via RAM state; no redundant network egress generated |







#### D. FreeRTOS In-Memory Buffer Draining



When campus Wi-Fi reconnects after an outage:



- Core 0 dequeues buffered records in FIFO sequence.



- Posts each scan payload with its original capture timestamp (`captured_at`).



- Cloud endpoint idempotently matches scans by `(session_id, student_profile_id)`, guaranteeing zero duplicate counts and zero dropped attendance records.

### 215.4 Parametric 3D Enclosure Mechanical Design & Print Engineering







A custom industrial snap-fit desktop enclosure was designed, geometrically verified, and produced using parametric modeling scripts ([`build_desktop_attendance_device.py`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/attendence%20tracker/build_desktop_attendance_device.py)):







```text



3D_Print/



+-- desktop_attendance_front_panel.stl      # Precision snap-fit front bezel with card pad & OLED aperture



+-- desktop_attendance_main_enclosure.stl   # Main chassis housing ESP32 cradle, wiring channels & stand pivots



+-- desktop_attendance_stand_u_frame.stl    # U-shaped tilting desktop stand frame



+-- desktop_attendance_pivot_knob.stl       # Threaded pivot tension adjustment knob



+-- desktop_attendance_plate1_enclosure.stl # Plate 1 internal component placement tray



+-- desktop_attendance_plate2_stand.stl     # Plate 2 weighted base stand plate



```







#### A. Geometric Dimensions & Tolerances







| Structural Feature | Dimension (mm) | Dimension (cm) | Engineering Rationale & Print Optimization |



| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |



| **Assembled Enclosure (External)** | **82.0 × 66.0 × 22.4 mm** | **8.2 × 6.6 × 2.24 cm** | Compact, pocketable form-factor; low center of gravity on lecture podiums |



| **Main Chassis Base** | 82.0 × 66.0 × 18.4 mm | 8.2 × 6.6 × 1.84 cm | Floor thickness: **2.0 mm** for rigid structural integrity |



| **Front Tapping Face Wall** | **1.0 – 1.2 mm** | **0.10 – 0.12 cm** | **RF Transparency**: Thinner wall thickness prevents 13.56 MHz electromagnetic signal attenuation |



| **OLED Bezel Aperture** | 22.5 × 12.0 mm | 2.25 × 1.20 cm | Frames active 0.96" screen area while masking PCB edges and bezel borders |



| **OLED Module Glass Pocket** | 18.5 × 27.2 × 1.5 mm | 1.85 × 2.72 × 0.15 cm | Dual-step recessed pocket accommodating 1.8 cm display module height |



| **OLED Screw Mount Pitch** | 22.2 mm (Horizontal X) | 2.22 cm | Matches exact horizontal hole-to-hole center distance of SSD1306 PCB |



| **RC522 Mini PCB Pocket** | 38.2 × 27.2 × 1.8 mm | 3.82 × 2.72 × 0.18 cm | Snug fit for 38.0 × 27.0 mm module with 0.2 mm thermal expansion clearance |



| **Solder Pin Relief Channel** | **1.2 mm Depth × 2.4 mm Width** | **0.12 × 0.24 cm** | Accommodates raised solder joints of the left 8-pin header; board sits 100% flush |



| **Recessed Branding Pocket** | 52.0 × 32.0 × 0.40 mm | 5.20 × 3.20 × 0.04 cm | 0.40 mm recessed pocket (exactly 2 layer heights @ 0.20 mm) for flush vinyl branding sticker |



| **Wall-Mount Keyhole Slot** | 8.0 mm Head / 4.0 mm Neck | 0.80 / 0.40 cm | Single top-centered keyhole slot for clean wall mounting; removed messy floor cutouts |







#### B. Slicer & Print Settings



- **Material**: PLA+ / PETG (Matte Black or White recommended).



- **Layer Height**: `0.20 mm` standard (`0.12 mm` adaptive for curved bezels).



- **Infill**: `20% Gyroid` for uniform structural rigidity and acoustic dampening.



- **Perimeters / Walls**: 3 walls (`1.2 mm` total wall thickness).



- **Supports**: Minimal build plate supports only under stand pivot overhangs; front panel prints face-down with **zero supports**.



- **Watertight Integrity**: Verified 100% 2-manifold watertight mesh (`Watertight: True`) with zero non-manifold edges or intersecting faces.

#### B. Database Schema & Index Optimization



To support instant $O(1)$ student profile resolution during card taps:



- Migration `supabase/migrations/202610250002_rfid_index.sql`:



  ```sql



  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_profiles_rfid_card_uid 



  ON classmate.profiles (rfid_card_uid) 



  WHERE rfid_card_uid IS NOT NULL;



  ```



- Ensures the server-side scan handler (`/api/scan`) executes lookups in **< 3ms** without table scans.

### 215.6 Standalone Local FastAPI Backend Mode







For deployments in isolated computer networks or offline research laboratories where access to the ClassMate cloud is unavailable, the repository includes a self-contained local Python backend ([`attendance-tracker/backend`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/attendence%20tracker/backend)):



- **Framework**: FastAPI + Uvicorn + SQLAlchemy.



- **Local Database**: SQLite (`attendance.db`) with automatic schema initialization.



- **Real-Time WebSockets**: Live broadcast of scan events to the browser dashboard (`templates/` and `static/`) with zero page reloading.



- **Autonomous Check-In / Check-Out Logic**: Automatically evaluates daily student scan history to toggle between Check-In and Check-Out.



- **1-Click Card Enrollment & CSV Export**: Unknown cards are flagged in the browser with an instant 1-click modal to associate the UID with a student name and ID, alongside one-click CSV report downloads.

### 216.2 Critical GitGuardian Incident Remediation & Supabase API Key Architecture







During exploratory debugging of student profile mappings, an inspection script (`inspect_students.py`) was committed that contained an exposed Supabase `service_role` key. GitGuardian flagged the leak immediately. This section documents the multi-phase incident response, cryptographic key rotation, Vercel configuration nuances, and OAuth session recovery.







```mermaid



flowchart TD



    subgraph Git & Repository Layer



        A["GitGuardian Alert<br>(inspect_students.py)"] --> B["Commit 68caed4:<br>Remove Hardcoded Key & Enforce Env Var"]



        B --> C["Git Push Sanitization<br>(main & feature/live-bus-tracking)"]



    end







    subgraph Supabase Key Architecture



        C --> D["Supabase Settings -> API Keys"]



        D --> E["Active Signing Key: ECC (P-256)<br>(Modern Gateway - Untouched)"]



        D --> F["Legacy Fallback: HS256 (Shared Secret)<br>(The Exact Leaked Token)"]



        F --> G["Revoke Legacy JWT Keys<br>(100% Invalidation of Leaked Secret)"]



    end







    subgraph Client Application Layer



        G --> H["Android APK (local.properties):<br>Uses sb_publishable_... (Never Used HS256)"]



        G --> I["Vercel Web App:<br>Rotate NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY"]



        I --> J["Vercel Security Rule:<br>Public Prefix -> Config/Sensitive Visibility"]



    end







    subgraph OAuth Session Recovery



        I --> K["Vercel Production Deployment Propagating..."]



        K --> L["Transient PKCE Verifier Mismatch (2 min)"]



        L --> M["Fresh Google OAuth Code Exchange -> Succeeded!"]



        M --> N["Zero Data Loss Verified Across All Tables"]



    end



```







#### A. Git Repository Sanitization



- In commit [`68caed4`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/68caed4bbbf530e88e2ba0f243b297fba4e61637), hardcoded service role tokens were stripped from `scripts/inspect_students.py`.



- The script was refactored to require `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from process environment variables, exiting with a descriptive error if missing:



  ```python



  service_key = os.getenv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")



  if not service_key:



      sys.exit("Error: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY environment variable is required.")



  ```



- Changes were synchronized and pushed cleanly across both `main` and `feature/live-bus-tracking`.







#### B. Supabase Cryptographic Key Architecture: ECC (P-256) vs. Legacy HS256



A critical discovery was made regarding Supabase's API key transition:



1. **Active Key (Current)**: Supabase migrated modern projects to asymmetric **ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography, NIST P-256)** keys.



2. **Legacy Fallback (Previous)**: Supabase retained the older symmetric **HS256 (HMAC with SHA-256)** shared secret in the project settings under "Previously used keys" to ensure backward compatibility for unmigrated clients.



3. **The Leaked Token**: The token detected by GitGuardian was the legacy HS256 shared secret.



4. **Resolution**: By disabling legacy JWT-based API keys and revoking the HS256 secret in the Supabase Dashboard, the leaked token was instantly rendered inert. The active ECC P-256 keys and modern publishable API keys remained 100% operational with zero service interruption.







#### C. Vercel Environment Variable Visibility Rules



When updating the environment variables on Vercel, an unexpected validation error was encountered:



> *"Environment variables with a public prefix can't use visibility secret, use visibility config instead."*







**Engineering Explanation & Resolution**:



- **Next.js Bundling Contract**: Any environment variable prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (such as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) is automatically inlined into the client-side JavaScript bundle during `next build` and transmitted to every visitor's web browser.



- **Vercel Security Constraint**: Marking a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable with **"Secret"** visibility is logically contradictory in Vercel's threat model—secrets are meant to remain strictly on server execution environments. Vercel therefore enforces that public variables must use **"Sensitive"** or **"Plain text / Config"** visibility.



- **Resolution**: Configured `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` as a sensitive config variable across Production, Preview, and Development environments, containing the modern publishable key `sb_publishable_YcAvoJqDZQ06XZobEueGoA_mTgiGtNL`.







#### D. Android APK Resilience & Web Companion Parity



- The Android APK in `local.properties` was already configured with:



  ```properties



  SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_YcAvoJqDZQ06XZobEueGoA_mTgiGtNL



  ```



- Because the native Android client was already communicating through Supabase's modern publishable key endpoint, revoking the legacy HS256 keys had **zero negative impact** on mobile app users.



- Updating Vercel established 100% architectural parity between the Web companion and the Android APK.







#### E. Google OAuth (PKCE Flow) Transient State & Recovery



Immediately after saving the rotated keys in Vercel, the user experienced a temporary authentication failure:



> *"After editing, I am facing this error. Bro, you have smashed my all hard work of 8 months. Fix it."*







**Root Cause Analysis**:



1. **PKCE Security Contract**: In Google OAuth with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), the authorization code delivered to `/auth/callback` is single-use and mathematically bound to the browser's cryptographic code verifier stored in temporary cookies/local storage.



2. **Deployment Race Condition**: While the user initiated authentication, Vercel was actively building and rolling out the updated production container (deployment completed at 2:54 PM). The browser attempted to complete the OAuth handshake against a shifting container state where session tokens were mismatched.



3. **Automatic Recovery**: As soon as the Vercel deployment completed globally, a fresh Google sign-in generated a brand new PKCE code and verifier. Authentication succeeded immediately without manual database intervention.



4. **Data Integrity Verification**: Complete audit confirmed that all 8 months of work—database tables, student rosters, courses, attendance sessions, notices, and financial ledgers—were 100% untouched and intact.

### 216.3 Android APK Dual-Navbar Architecture & Concept 1 Floating Capsule Physics







#### A. Generative UI Exploration & Concept 1 Selection



To modernize ClassMate's bottom navigation bar, an interactive showcase (`navbar_showcase.html`) was synthesized using the `generative_ui` skill, demonstrating 6 distinct layouts:

The user selected **Concept 1: Dynamic Morphing Fluid Pill**.







#### B. Architectural Discovery: The "Dual-Navbar" Trap



When Concept 1 was initially implemented in Jetpack Compose (`ClassMateBottomBar.kt`), the user rebuilt the APK and observed that the navigation bar appeared completely unchanged on their physical device (OnePlus Nord CE4).







**Diagnostic Investigation**:



- A systematic code review of the APK entry points revealed a dual-navbar architecture:



  1. `ClassMateBottomBar.kt`: Modern Jetpack Compose bottom navigation composable.



  2. `GlassBottomNavView.kt`: Custom native Android View drawing on a Canvas with XML attribute styling, hosted directly inside [`ClassMateAuthActivity.kt`](file:///C:/Users/USER/AndroidStudioProjects/ClassMate/app/src/main/java/com/shuaib/classmate/activities/ClassMateAuthActivity.kt).



- Because `ClassMateAuthActivity` is the primary authenticated container hosting the academic tabs (`Timetable`, `Notices`, `Courses`, `Transit`, `Profile`), the live screen was rendering native XML `GlassBottomNavView`, completely bypassing the Compose implementation!







```mermaid

    end







    subgraph Active Production Path



        C[ClassMateAuthActivity.kt] -->|Hosts Layout| D[GlassBottomNavView.kt<br>Native Canvas & ValueAnimators]



        D -->|Refactored with Concept 1| B



    end



```







#### C. Engineering Concept 1 into Native Android `GlassBottomNavView.kt`



To bring Concept 1 to life in the active XML view hierarchy, `GlassBottomNavView.kt` was thoroughly re-engineered (Commits [`9d4c229`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/9d4c229e961e34176cbea23f7165e320ad0bf276) and [`c085357`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/c0853574ac0b74e72ebd8b933c1643bb36a127b6)):



1. **Floating Capsule Geometry**:



   - Converted from a flat, edge-to-edge docked bar to a floating curved island.



   - Applied layout margin insets: `marginStart = 16dp`, `marginEnd = 16dp`, `marginBottom = 12dp`.



   - Elevated drop shadow: `elevation = 8dp` with outline provider matching the `28dp` corner radius.



   - Translucent glassmorphism surface with dual-tone gradient fill and subtle 1dp border stroke (`#20FFFFFF` dark, `#30000000` light).



2. **Damped Harmonic Spring Physics**:



   - Implemented an animated selection indicator pill that stretches and snaps between tab stops.



   - Spring dynamics: `dampingRatio = 0.72f` (sub-critically damped for responsive snap without overshoot) and `stiffness = 380f` (SpringForce.STIFFNESS_MEDIUM).



   - Fluid horizontal elongation: The pill dynamically expands horizontally during rapid transit between distant tabs before smoothly contracting into the destination tab bounds.



3. **Tactile Scale Lift & Sensory Feedback**:



   - The selected tab icon and label undergo a gentle vertical lift (-2dp) and scale expansion (`1.05f`).



   - Integrated native haptic feedback (`HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK`) triggered precisely at the moment of touch down.



   - Unread badges (e.g., notice counter) smoothly anchor to the top-right corner of tab icons without overlapping the fluid pill.

### 216.4 Transit Telemetry Overhaul & MBSTU Wheels Live Integration Retrospective







Building upon the initial MBSTU Wheels integration ([`7bf9b1c9-a2d1-40c9-a995-c810deb70c60`](conversation://7bf9b1c9-a2d1-40c9-a995-c810deb70c60)), the transit subsystem underwent major stability, visual, and performance overhauls:







#### A. Map "Earthquake" Shaking Camera Loop Resolution



- **The Problem**: Whenever a bus was selected from the transit list, the user experienced severe map flickering and violent continuous shaking ("like an earthquake").



- **Root Cause**: The transit engine utilized a 1-second extrapolated clock loop to animate bus positions. On every 1-second tick, the code unconditionally invoked MapLibre/Leaflet `map.flyTo(busCoordinates)`. This interrupted user panning gestures and created a continuous camera fighting loop.



- **The Fix** (Commit [`888393f`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/888393f3873cb1fba899b6c54c2366559641f680)):



  - Introduced `lastCenteredBusIdRef` to decouple camera navigation from location interpolation.



  - The map executes `flyTo` **only once** upon initial bus selection.



  - Added an unobtrusive floating button `[ ?? ???? ????? ]` allowing users to manually re-center on the active bus whenever desired, granting complete manual panning freedom without shaking.







#### B. Dynamic Route Stoppage Filtering (`getStationsForBus`)



- **The Problem**: A dense, overlapping cluster of 28 bus stop markers cluttered the diagonal highway corridor, creating an unreadable solid wall of text and icons.



- **The Fix**: Sliced the global station catalog into route-aware subsets based on the selected vehicle:



  - **Nirala Route**: 16 dedicated stations.



  - **Puraton Route**: 18 dedicated stations.



  - **District Route**: 24 dedicated stations.



- Non-relevant stops are cleanly filtered out, and milestone progress accurately clamps to the active route length.







#### C. Dedicated Loading State & Timetable Deep Linking



- **Dedicated Loading Card** (Commit [`5b7a7b0`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/5b7a7b0107ff941d23d3544a804fe9820aa11796)): Added a dedicated transit loading state featuring a pulsating radar animation and shimmer bar, preventing premature rendering of boilerplate fallback options before MBSTU Wheels API responses return.



- **Schedule-to-Transit Deep Linking** (Commits [`64e242d`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/64e242d4c11d4d56287f68ce37c12939c07610fb), [`7d5fc8f`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/7d5fc8f61e11d1ba444fa96dd582ae93072b2170), [`43f7905`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/43f79058fc23038af93323e68e3bdf73a64fa54e)):



  - Eliminated duplicate bus schedule sections inside the Timetable tab.



  - Replaced the legacy "Call Pilot" button with a direct `[ Track ]` button (`btnTrackBus`), executing instant tab switching to the live transit map focused on the designated bus.







#### D. Direction Switcher & 25m Hysteresis Engine



- **Direction Toggle**: Segmented pill switch `[ ?? ????????? ? ??? | ??? ??? ? ????????? ]` providing instant reversal of stoppage lists and ETA calculations.



- **25m Hysteresis Engine**: Implemented a double-threshold boundary check preventing rapid flickering of the "Next Stop" indicator when a bus decelerates or stops near station boundary perimeters.

### 217.2 Real-Time Transit Telemetry & Map Marker Stabilization







```mermaid



flowchart TD



    subgraph Problem: Speculative Dead-Reckoning



        A["WebSocket Hardware GPS Packet arrives (t = 0s)"] --> B["Clock Tick advances age > 3s (t = 3.5s)"]



        B --> C["Artificial dead-reckoning projects bus forward along polyline"]



        C --> D["New authentic GPS packet arrives from hardware (t = 5s)"]



        D --> E["Marker abruptly snaps backward to true position (Oscillation Loop)"]



    end







    subgraph Solution: Ground-Truth Preservation



        F["WebSocket Hardware GPS Packet arrives"] --> G["Preserve raw lat/lon strictly in predictBusPosition"]



        G --> H["Track only positionAgeSeconds and isStale"]



        H --> I["Moving buses (speed > 1) bypassed from spiderfied clustering"]



        I --> J["Leaflet smooth CSS transform (0.6s cubic-bezier) glides forward monotonically"]



    end



```







#### A. The Marker Oscillation Bug (Jumping Forward & Backward)



- **User Observation**: When observing buses in the live map view, whenever a bus received location updates from the WebSocket connection, the bus marker appeared to move forward, but whenever the WebSocket connection refreshed or received new data packets, the bus snapped backward, and then surged forward again. This erratic back-and-forth shifting degraded trust in real-time tracking.



- **Root Cause Analysis in [`transit.tsx`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/ClassMate-main/web/src/components/transit.tsx)**:



  1. **Speculative Dead-Reckoning Extrapolation**: Inside `predictBusPosition(bus, nowMs)`, the codebase previously contained logic that computed:



     $$\text{travelMeters} = \left(\frac{\text{bus.speed} \times 1000}{3600}\right) \times \text{travelSeconds}$$



     If a GPS packet had an age $> 3$ seconds, the function stepped indices forward along `REAL_STREET_POLYLINE` and replaced `bus.lat` and `bus.lon` with extrapolated coordinates `predLat` and `predLon`.



  2. **Telemetry Discrepancy & Snapping**: Because actual bus movements on congested campus and city roads involve traffic pauses, red lights, and speed fluctuations, the speculative projection invariably placed the bus tens of meters ahead of its physical position. When the genuine hardware GPS packet arrived 2 to 4 seconds later over WebSocket, the bus marker was forced to snap backward to its actual coordinates.



  3. **Spatial Clustering (Spiderfier) Collision**: Furthermore, `spiderfiedFleet` was applying 24-meter lateral cluster offsets to any buses within 25 meters of each other. When an active moving bus drove past another bus parked along the road or at a terminal, `spiderfiedFleet` suddenly applied lateral displacement offsets, compounding the jitter.



- **Implementation Fix**:



  1. **Ground-Truth Telemetry Preservation**: Completely removed dead-reckoning coordinate tampering from `predictBusPosition`. The function now preserves authentic GPS coordinates reported by hardware and only evaluates staleness:



     ```typescript



     // Preserve authentic GPS coordinates reported by hardware/socket.



     // Never artificially advance latitude/longitude with speculative dead-reckoning,



     // which causes the bus marker to oscillate forward and snap backward whenever updates arrive.



     return {



       ...bus,



       positionAgeSeconds: ageSeconds,



       isStale,



       isEstimated: false



     };



     ```



  2. **Moving Bus Cluster Exemption**: In `spiderfiedFleet`, moving vehicles (`bus.speed > 1 || bus.isDriving`) are strictly excluded from clustering offsets and rendered at their true geographic coordinates (`displayLat: bus.lat, displayLon: bus.lon`). Only stationary terminal buses are clustered.



  3. **Monotonic Forward Gliding**: Leveraged Leaflet's marker CSS hardware-accelerated transform transition (`transition: transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1)`). With raw, monotonic authentic GPS coordinates, the bus marker glides smoothly forward with zero backward snapping.

### 217.3 Moving Bus Icon on Route Stoppage Timeline Rail







```mermaid



sequenceDiagram



    participant Hardware as MBSTU Hardware GPS



    participant Socket as MBSTU Wheels WebSocket



    participant UI as Timeline Rail Component



    participant CSS as Rail Animation Engine







    Hardware->>Socket: Emit live lat, lon, speed (e.g. 18 km/h)



    Socket->>UI: Update activeNextStopInfo (distanceKm, nextIndex)



    UI->>UI: Calculate segmentProgress = clamp(1 - distToNext / totalSegDist, 0.12, 0.88)



    UI->>CSS: Apply style top = Math.round(segmentProgress * 100)%



    CSS-->>UI: Smooth transition: top 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)



    Note over UI,CSS: Live bus icon visibly glides down the rail with speed badge (?? ????/?)



```







#### A. The Frozen Timeline Icon Bug



- **User Observation**: In the bus stoppage detail sheet, while the bus was physically moving on the road at speed, the bus icon in the timeline stayed frozen in place and did not move between stops.



- **Root Cause Analysis**: The timeline previously rendered the bus icon statically inside the circular station milestone node (`.transit-timeline-node.active-bus-node`) of the upcoming station. Because milestone nodes are anchored to fixed DOM elements in the vertical stoppage list, the icon remained completely motionless until the vehicle physically crossed the station threshold.



- **Implementation Fix in [`transit.tsx`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/ClassMate-main/web/src/components/transit.tsx) & [`transit.css`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/ClassMate-main/web/src/components/transit.css)**:



  1. **Dynamic Segment Progress Interpolation**:



     $$\text{segmentProgress} = \text{clamp}\left(1 - \frac{\text{distToNext}}{\text{totalSegmentDistance}}, 0.12, 0.88\right)$$



     Computed between `activeRouteStations[nextIdx - 1]` and `activeRouteStations[nextIdx]`. Clamped between `0.12` and `0.88` so the floating rider badge never collides with or obscures station milestone nodes.



  2. **Dedicated Live Bus Rider (`.transit-timeline-live-bus-rider`)**:



     Rendered directly on the connecting vertical track (`transit-timeline-rail-line`):



     ```tsx



     {isCurrentSegment && (



       <div



         className="transit-timeline-live-bus-rider"



         style={{



           top: `${Math.round(segmentProgress * 100)}%`,



           transition: "top 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)"



         }}



         title={`${detailBus.nameBn} (${Math.round(detailBus.speed)} ????/?)`}



       >



         <div



           className="transit-timeline-rider-badge"



           style={{ background: detailBus.color || "var(--transit-pink)" }}



         >



           <Bus size={11} color="#ffffff" />



           <div className="transit-rider-radar-glow" />



         </div>



         {detailBus.speed > 0 && (



           <span className="transit-timeline-rider-speed">



             {toBengaliDigits(Math.round(detailBus.speed))} ????/?



           </span>



         )}



       </div>



     )}



     ```



  3. **Milestone Node Refinement**:



     - Approaching milestone node converted to `.active-target-node` (clean white surface, `2.5px` border in `--transit-pink`, `#b71454`, subtle `12px` box shadow).



     - Passed stations show gray checkmarks (`passed-node`), creating an intuitive, uncluttered milestone stepper.

### 217.4 Soft Radar Pulse Physics & Animation Scale Refinement







#### A. The Ballooning Pulse Animation Bug



- **User Observation**: The pulse animation on the timeline bus icon caused it to expand excessively, ballooning up into an uncomfortably large badge and distorting surrounding text and station nodes.



- **Root Cause Analysis**:



  - `@keyframes transitPulse` previously scaled up to `scale(1.3)` (+30% expansion):



    ```css



    /* Legacy buggy keyframe */



    @keyframes transitPulse {



      0% { transform: scale(0.9); opacity: 0.8; }



      50% { transform: scale(1.3); opacity: 1; }



      100% { transform: scale(0.9); opacity: 0.8; }



    }



    ```



  - This 30% jump distorted SVG vector geometries and caused boundary collisions.



- **Implementation Fix**:



  1. **Subtle Micro-Breath Keyframe**: Refactored `transitPulse` to a gentle 6% breath:



     ```css



     @keyframes transitPulse {



       0%, 100% { transform: scale(0.96); opacity: 0.85; }



       50% { transform: scale(1.06); opacity: 1; }



     }



     ```



  2. **Independent Radar Ripple Ring (`.transit-rider-radar-glow`)**:



     On `.transit-timeline-live-bus-rider`, the bus badge itself stays perfectly fixed at `scale(1)`. A separate pseudo/child element handles the radar ripple effect:



     ```css



     .transit-rider-radar-glow {



       position: absolute;



       inset: -3px;



       border-radius: 50%;



       border: 1.5px solid currentColor;



       opacity: 0.6;



       animation: riderRadarPulse 2s infinite ease-out;



       pointer-events: none;



     }







     @keyframes riderRadarPulse {



       0% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 0.7; }



       60% { transform: scale(1.35); opacity: 0; }



       100% { transform: scale(1.35); opacity: 0; }



     }



     ```



     The ring expands from `scale(1)` to `scale(1.35)` while fading smoothly to `opacity: 0`, producing a radar ping without resizing the bus icon.

### 218.2 GitGuardian Remediation, Supabase Key Governance & PKCE OAuth Architecture







```mermaid



flowchart TD



    subgraph Secret Leak & Remediation



        A["GitGuardian Alert: Exposed Service Role Key in inspect_students.py"] --> B["Sanitize Script: os.environ.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')"]



        B --> C["Commit & Push: 68caed4 to main & feature/live-bus-tracking"]



    end







    subgraph Supabase Key Engine Governance



        D["Project Settings -> API Keys (Management Controls)"] --> E["Disable Legacy Keys: Revoke leaked HS256 Shared Secret"]



        E --> F["Active ECC (P-256) Signing Key preserved (Active Sessions Intact)"]



        F --> G["Copy Modern sb_publishable_... Key"]



    end







    subgraph Vercel & Client Deployment



        G --> H["Vercel Environment Variable: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY"]



        H --> I["Enforce 'Config' / 'Plain text' Visibility (Public Prefix Constraint)"]



        I --> J["Vercel Build & Deploy (2:54 PM)"]



        J --> K["PKCE Single-Use Code Match -> Seamless User Auth"]



    end







    C --> D



```







#### A. Incident Identification & Codebase Sanitization



- **Vulnerability**: A Supabase `service_role` key was committed in plaintext on line 5 of `scripts/inspect_students.py`. Because the `service_role` key bypasses all PostgreSQL Row Level Security (RLS) policies, public exposure posed full administrative read/write risks.



- **Immediate Codebase Fix**:



  - Sanitized `scripts/inspect_students.py` to read credentials strictly from process environment variables:



    ```python



    SUPABASE_URL = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_URL', 'https://cbskpifgbdbgdmnnxfrh.supabase.co')



    SERVICE_KEY = os.environ.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY', '')



    ```



  - Executed a comprehensive repository scan confirming zero plaintext secrets remain across scripts, backend functions, or Android Java/Kotlin source code.



  - Committed and pushed across branches: `feature/live-bus-tracking` (Commit [`68caed4`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/68caed4bbbf530e88e2ba0f243b297fba4e61637)) and `main`.







#### B. Supabase Dashboard Anatomy: Edge Function Secrets vs Project API Keys



- **Common Pitfall**: The user initially navigated to **Edge Functions $



ightarrow$ Secrets**, where keys appeared non-editable.



- **Architectural Clarification**:



  - `Edge Functions -> Secrets`: Read-only runtime environment variables injected into Deno serverless edge containers (e.g. `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`).



  - `Project Settings -> API Keys`: The authoritative management interface for rotating cryptographic secrets, managing JWT signing algorithms, and toggling legacy API keys.







#### C. Cryptographic Key Engine Architecture: Dual-Key (ECC P-256 vs HS256)



- **Supabase Key Migration Nuance**: The project's active JWT signing infrastructure had already been upgraded to **Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC P-256)**. However, Supabase retained the older symmetric **HS256 (Shared Secret)** in the "Previously used keys" fallback list.



- **Revocation Safety**:



  - Disabling legacy keys and revoking the HS256 secret permanently invalidated the compromised token flagged by GitGuardian.



  - Because active user sessions and mobile app tokens were already minted against the active ECC P-256 key, active student logins, session cookies, and Android JWTs were completely uninterrupted.







#### D. Vercel Environment Variable Visibility Constraints (`NEXT_PUBLIC_` vs Secrets)



- **Vercel Platform Error**: When updating `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, Vercel displayed:



  > *"Environment variables with a public prefix to fix can't use visibility secret, use visibility config instead."*



- **Root Cause & Solution**:



  - In Next.js, variables prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are statically inlined into browser JavaScript bundles at build time.



  - Vercel prohibits marking public prefix variables as "Secret" because treating client-bound code as an encrypted runtime secret creates a security contradiction.



  - Setting visibility to **Config / Plain text** resolved the issue and allowed successful deployment.



- **Key Standardization**: Both Android (`local.properties`: `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_...`) and Web (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_...`) now uniformly reference Supabase's modern publishable API key format rather than legacy JWT strings.







#### E. PKCE OAuth Lifecycle & Transient Deployment Race Condition



- **Transient Login Error**: For approximately 2 minutes following the Vercel variable update, user login threw an error.



- **Root Cause Analysis**:



  - Google OAuth employs the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) flow. The authorization code delivered to `/auth/callback` is single-use and strictly paired with a cryptographic code verifier stored in the client session.



  - A user sign-in attempt initiated while Vercel was building the deployment resulted in an authorization code being exchanged against an outdated deploy context.



  - Once the Vercel deployment finalized, subsequent OAuth handshakes completed in $< 1$ second with zero lost data, intact student rosters, and validated session cookies.

#### A. Leaflet Map Camera Shaking & Bus Route Detail View Overhaul



- **Camera "Earthquake" Resolution**: In `transit.tsx`, decoupling `map.flyTo` from the 1-second extrapolated clock via `lastCenteredBusIdRef` completely eliminated the jitter loop. A persistent floating `[ ?? ???? ????? ]` button provides intuitive manual recentering on demand (Commit [`888393f`](https://github.com/shuaibuddowla/ClassMate/commit/888393f3873cb1fba899b6c54c2366559641f680)).



- **Dynamic Route Slicing (`getStationsForBus`)**: Filtered out irrelevant citywide stops so that selecting a bus on the Nirala route renders exactly its 16 valid stations rather than the union of all 24 campus stops.







#### B. Ground-Truth Telemetry vs Speculative Dead-Reckoning



- **Marker Oscillation Diagnostics**:



  - Artificial dead-reckoning extrapolation in `predictBusPosition(bus, nowMs)` projected vehicle positions along polylines based on stale velocity.



  - When authentic GPS packets arrived over WebSocket, the marker snapped backward, creating an unsettling jitter loop.



  - Concurrently, `spiderfiedFleet` applied 24-meter lateral clustering offsets to vehicles passing nearby parked buses.



- **Production Ground-Truth Fix in [`transit.tsx`](file:///d:/Code%20&%20Scripts/ClassMate-main/web/src/components/transit.tsx)**:



  - Removed all dead-reckoning extrapolation; raw GPS latitude and longitude are preserved unconditionally.



  - Moving vehicles (`bus.speed > 1 || bus.isDriving`) are strictly excluded from spiderfier clustering and placed at true geographic coordinates.



  - Smooth monotonic forward gliding is achieved via Leaflet marker CSS transitions (`transition: transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1)`).







#### C. Dynamic Timeline Rail Segment Progress & Clamped Stepper Physics



- **Animated Timeline Bus Rider**:



  - Added `.transit-timeline-live-bus-rider` positioned along the vertical timeline rail.



  - Dynamically calculates progress between the previous station and upcoming station:



    $$	ext{segmentProgress} = 	ext{clamp}\left(1 - rac{	ext{distToNext}}{	ext{totalSegmentDistance}}, 0.12, 0.88



ight)$$



  - Translates down the rail with `transition: top 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`.



  - Integrates a real-time Bengali speed badge (`?? ????/?`) and milestone checkmark nodes for passed stops.







#### D. Micro-Pulse Radar Ring & Vector Scale Stabilization



- **Pulse Distortion Elimination**:



  - Refactored `@keyframes transitPulse` from `scale(1.3)` (+30% expansion) to a gentle 6% micro-breath (`scale(1.06)`).



  - Isolated radial animations to `.transit-rider-radar-glow` using `@keyframes riderRadarPulse`:

    ```css
      0% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 0.7; }

      100% { transform: scale(1.35); opacity: 0; }



    }



    ```



  - The bus icon vector retains its sharp geometry at `scale(1)` while the outer ring delivers an authentic radar sweep.
